children.translated_text: <s>Caitanya</s> (consciousness) is the <s>Ātman</s> (Self). // SivS 1.1 //

body.translated_text: <s>Śivasūtra</s>, First <s>Unmeṣa</s> (Awakening)

children.text: * caitanyaṃ citkriyārūpaṃ śivasya paramasya yat || SivSV_1.1:1 ||
children.translated_text: * The <s>caitanya</s> (consciousness) which is the nature of the activity of awareness (<s>citkriyā</s>) of the supreme <s>Śiva</s>

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]

body.text: * svātantryam etad evātmā tato 'sau paramaḥ śivaḥ || SivSV_1.1:2 ||
body.translated_text: * this very freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>) is the <s>Ātman</s>; therefore He is the supreme <s>Śiva</s>.

body.text: * athavā ko 'yam ātmeti praṣṭ bodhayituṃ śiśūn || SivSV_1.1:3 ||
body.translated_text: * Or, to instruct the students who ask 'What is this <s>Ātman</s>?'

body.text: * nātmā deho na ca prāṇo na manaḥ khaṃ na śūnyabhūḥ || SivSV_1.1:4 ||
body.translated_text: * The <s>Ātman</s> is not the body, not the vital breath (<s>prāṇa</s>), not the mind, not space, not the void;

body.text: * kiṃtu caitanyam evātmety ādiṣṭaṃ parameṣṭhinā || SivSV_1.1:5 ||
body.translated_text: * but consciousness alone is the <s>Ātman</s> — thus it is taught by the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameṣṭhin</s>).

body.text: * atha caitanyam evaitad ātmā svābhāvikaṃ vapuḥ || SivSV_1.1:6 ||
body.translated_text: * Furthermore, this very <s>caitanya</s> (consciousness) is the <s>Ātman</s>, the natural form

body.text: * viśeṣācodanād asya jagataś cety arūpiṇaḥ || SivSV_1.1:7 ||
body.translated_text: * of this formless universe, as indicated by specific injunction.

body.text: * acetyamānaṃ kasyāpi vapuḥ kim api no bhavet || SivSV_1.1:8 ||
body.translated_text: * A form not cognized by anyone would not exist at all;

body.text: * cetyamānaṃ tu cidrūpatādātmyāc cinmayaṃ bhavet || SivSV_1.1:9 ||
body.translated_text: * but what is cognized, through identity with the nature of consciousness, becomes of the nature of consciousness (<s>cinmaya</s>).
* Thus, by the principle taught by <s>Śiva</s>, of both the moving and the stationary beings,

body.text: * caitanyam eva viśvasya svarūpaṃ pāramārthikam || SivSV_1.1:11 ||
body.translated_text: * consciousness alone is the ultimate true nature of the universe.

body.text: * nanv evaṃvidhaviśvasya caitanyaṃ ced vapus tadā || SivSV_1.1:12 ||
body.translated_text: * Now, if consciousness is the form of such a universe, then

body.text: * kathaṃ bandhasya sambandha iti śaṅkāṃ vyapohitum || SivSV_1.1:13 ||
body.translated_text: * to dispel the doubt 'How can there be a connection with bondage?'
* the Great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>) states the <s>sūtra</s> through two readings: with conjunction and without conjunction.]
<s>Jñāna</s> (limited knowledge) is bondage. // SivS 1.2 //

children.translated_text: * First, in the Self whose nature is the expansion of consciousness (<s>caitanyasphāra</s>), ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) —

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]

body.text: * ātmany anātmatājñānaṃ jñānaṃ punar anātmani || SivSV_1.2:2 ||
body.translated_text: * in the Self, the ignorance of non-selfhood; and knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) again in the non-self,

body.text: * dehādāv ātmamānitvaṃ dvayam apy etad āṇavam || SivSV_1.2:3 ||
body.translated_text: * the false identification of the body etc. as the Self — both of these are <s>āṇava</s> (innate impurity);

body.text: * malaṃ svakalpitaṃ svasmin bandhaḥ svecchāvibhāvitaḥ || SivSV_1.2:4 ||
body.translated_text: * impurity (<s>mala</s>) self-created within oneself, bondage manifested by one's own will.

body.text: * kim āṇavamalātmaiva bandho 'yaṃ nety udīryate || SivSV_1.2:5 ||]
body.translated_text: * Is this bondage solely of the nature of <s>āṇava mala</s> (innate impurity) or not? It is stated:]
The womb (<s>yoni</s>) and the group (<s>varga</s>, of <s>tattvas</s>), the body of <s>kalā</s>. // SivS 1.3 //

children.text: * yonir bhedaprathāhetur māyā vargas tadutthitaḥ || SivSV_1.3:1 ||
children.translated_text: * The womb (<s>yoni</s>) is <s>Māyā</s>, the cause of the manifestation of differentiation; the group (<s>varga</s>) arises from that,

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]
* the collection of <s>tattvas</s> from <s>kalā</s> to earth, constituting that (body).
* The impurity called <s>māyīya</s> consists of the manifestation of differentiated objects;

body.text: * kaleti kāyam āviśya paricchedakarī nṛṇām || SivSV_1.3:4 ||
body.translated_text: * <s>Kalā</s>, entering the body, creates limitation in beings.

body.text: * vyāpṛtiḥ puṇyapāpātmā śarīraṃ yasya tat punaḥ || SivSV_1.3:5 ||
body.translated_text: * The activity consisting of merit and demerit (<s>puṇya</s> and <s>pāpa</s>), whose body that is, furthermore

body.text: * kārmaṃ ca malam etasmin dvaye bandho 'nuvartate || SivSV_1.3:6 ||
body.translated_text: * is the <s>kārma mala</s> (action-based impurity); in these two (<s>māyīya</s> and <s>kārma</s>), bondage persists.
* This triad of impurities (<s>malatrayam</s>) has been stated in the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s>:
* The loss of freedom of awareness, and the lack of awareness of freedom —
* this <s>āṇava mala</s> is twofold, through the robbery of one's own true nature.
* The manifestation of differentiated objects alone is the <s>māyīya</s> (impurity), giving rise to birth and experience;

body.text: * kartary abodhe kārmaṃ tu māyāśaktyaiva tat trayam || SivSV_1.3:11 ||
body.translated_text: * when the agent is unaware, there is <s>kārma</s> (action impurity); that triad arises through <s>māyāśakti</s> alone.

body.text: * ity athaiṣāṃ malānāṃ tu bandhakatvaṃ nirūpyate || SivSV_1.3:12 ||]
body.translated_text: * Thus the bondage-producing nature of these impurities is now examined.]
The foundation of (limited) knowledge is <s>Mātṛkā</s> (the alphabet-mother). // SivS 1.4 //

children.translated_text: * Incomplete, of the nature of otherness, consisting of the manifestation of differentiated objects,

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]
* having the form of all the impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) of auspicious and inauspicious <s>karma</s>,

body.text: * trividhaṃ malam uktaṃ yat tad eva jñānam ucyate || SivSV_1.4:3 ||
body.translated_text: * that which has been described as the threefold impurity — that very thing is called (limited) knowledge.

body.text: * na so 'sti pratyayo loke yaḥ śabdānugamād ṛte || SivSV_1.4:4 ||
body.translated_text: * There is no cognition (<s>pratyaya</s>) in the world without the accompaniment of word (<s>śabda</s>);

body.text: * anuviddham iva jñānaṃ sarvaṃ śabdena gamyate || SivSV_1.4:5 ||
body.translated_text: * all knowledge is understood as if pervaded by word.

body.text: * ity uktanītyā jñānasya vividhasyāsya mātṛkā || SivSV_1.4:6 ||
body.translated_text: * Thus, by the stated principle, of this manifold knowledge, <s>Mātṛkā</s>
* having the form of fifty phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>) from 'a' to 'kṣa'
* is the birthplace of the collection of <s>tattvas</s> from <s>Śiva</s> down to earth.
* Stationed in the midst of the awareness of the senses, supporting the bonds of <s>Brahmā</s>,
* the <s>Pīṭheśvarīs</s> (goddesses of the sacred seats), terrifying, delude again and again.
* Thus, following the principle stated in the <s>Śrītimirodghāṭa</s>,
* adorned by the circle of mothers (<s>mātṛcakra</s>) presiding over the groups beginning with vowels:

body.text: * apūrṇo 'ham ahaṃ pūrṇo 'haṃ kṛśo 'haṃ kṛśetaraḥ || SivSV_1.4:13 ||
body.translated_text: * 'I am incomplete,' 'I am complete,' 'I am thin,' 'I am stout' —
* thus through the pervasion of words, (the <s>Mātṛkā</s>) produces grief, joy, and so forth.
* As foundation and ruler, through that ruling over beings,
* those (cognitions) that have not attained inward-facing repose in one's own Self, continuously
* outward-turned cognitions are said to be the causes of bondage.
* Now the means for the pacification of such bondage-connection is stated
* by the Supreme Lord, having the reality of repose in the supreme goal:]
The arising (<s>udyama</s>) is <s>Bhairava</s>. // SivS 1.5 //

children.translated_text: * That which, of one's own awareness (<s>svasaṃvid</s>) expanding in the form of reflective consciousness (<s>vimarśa</s>),

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]
* has the nature of a sudden upsurge, a flash of insight (<s>pratibhā</s>) emerging,
* this arising (<s>udyama</s>) is the inner vibration (<s>parispanda</s>), having the nature of full I-consciousness (<s>pūrṇāhambhāvanā</s>).

body.text: * sa eva sarvaśaktīnāṃ sāmarasyād aśeṣataḥ || SivSV_1.5:4 ||
body.translated_text: * That very one, through the coalescence (<s>sāmarasya</s>) of all powers (<s>śaktis</s>) completely,
* by being filled from all sides, of the differentiating thought-constructs (<s>vikalpas</s>)

body.text: * alaṃ kavalanenāpīty anvarthād eva bhairavaḥ || SivSV_1.5:6 ||
body.translated_text: * is capable of devouring (them) — hence etymologically He is <s>Bhairava</s> (the awe-inspiring one).
* Now, from such attainment of the <s>Bhairava</s> state, which is the cause of the pacification of bondage,

body.text: * vyutthānaṃ ca bhavec chāntabhedābhāsam itīryate || SivSV_1.5:8 ||]
body.translated_text: * even the state of ordinary consciousness (<s>vyutthāna</s>) becomes one in which the appearance of difference is pacified — thus it is stated.]
In the union with the circle of powers (<s>śakticakra</s>), dissolution of the universe (occurs). // SivS 1.6 //

children.text: * yo 'yam uktaḥ svasaṃvitter udyamo bhairavātmakaḥ || SivSV_1.6:1 ||
children.translated_text: * This arising of one's own awareness which has been described as having the nature of <s>Bhairava</s>

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]
* has a great power (<s>śakti</s>) that transcends both sequential and non-sequential approaches;
* it is eager to pervade the complete circle of one's own consciousness-powers (<s>cicchakticakra</s>).
* Though appearing as empty, non-empty, both, or neither — it is the supreme (<s>parā</s>);
* by which alone, upon the canvas of one's own consciousness, beginning with the manifestation of objects,
* having the form of vibration (<s>spanda</s>) extending up to repose in the supreme subject (<s>parapramātṛ</s>),
* through the extension of the powers of manifestation called creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>), maintenance (<s>sthiti</s>), and dissolution (<s>laya</s>),
* the fivefold activity (<s>pañcakṛtya</s>) operating in the phenomenal world is manifested.

body.text: * tayā prasāritasyāsya śakticakrasya yat punaḥ || SivSV_1.6:9 ||
body.translated_text: * Of this circle of powers (<s>śakticakra</s>) extended by that (supreme power), what further
* union (<s>saṃdhāna</s>) is — it is the contemplation of the sequence taught in the inner tradition (<s>āntarāmnāya</s>).

body.text: * tasmin saty asya viśvasya kālāgnyādikalāvadheḥ || SivSV_1.6:11 ||
body.translated_text: * When that (union) exists, of this universe extending from the fire of time (<s>kālāgni</s>) to the boundary of <s>kalā</s>,
* dissolution occurs, characterized by the reality of the fire of one's own awareness.
* Thus for the <s>yogin</s> whose (sense of) difference has been burned by the fire of time of one's own awareness,

body.text: * na syāt samādhivyutthānabhedaḥ ko 'pīti kathyate || SivSV_1.6:14 ||
body.translated_text: * there would be no distinction whatsoever between <s>samādhi</s> and ordinary consciousness (<s>vyutthāna</s>) — so it is stated.
* In the differentiation of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, the experience of the fourth state (<s>turya</s>) arises;

body.text: * udyamo bhairava iti proktarūpaṃ sphuradvapuḥ || SivSV_1.6:16 ||
body.translated_text: * 'The arising is <s>Bhairava</s>' — such is the stated form, the flashing forth.

body.text: * turyaṃ nāma paraṃ dhāma tadābhogaś camatkriyā || SivSV_1.6:17 ||
body.translated_text: * <s>Turya</s> (the fourth) is the supreme abode; its experience is the activity of wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>).

body.text: * bhede 'pi jāgradādīnāṃ yoginas tasya sambhavaḥ || SivSV_1.6:18 ||
body.translated_text: * Even in the differentiation of waking and the other (states), for the <s>yogin</s>, its manifestation

body.text: * anusyūtiḥ parānandarūpā syād iti śiṣyate || SivSV_1.6:19 ||
body.translated_text: * becomes a continuous pervasion (<s>anusyūti</s>) of the nature of supreme bliss (<s>parānanda</s>) — thus it is taught.
* The triad of waking and the others is indicated sequentially by three <s>sūtras</s>:]
<s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge through external senses) is the waking state. // SivS 1.7 //
Dreaming is thought-constructs (<s>vikalpas</s>). // SivS 1.8 //
Non-discrimination (<s>aviveka</s>) is <s>Māyā</s>, the state of deep sleep. // SivS 1.9 //

children.translated_text: * Knowledge born of the external senses is waking, having objects common to all;

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]

body.text: * svapnaḥ svātmaiva samprokto vikalpāḥ svātmasambhavāḥ || SivSV_1.9:2 ||
body.translated_text: * dreaming is declared to be the self alone; thought-constructs (<s>vikalpas</s>) arise from one's own self.

body.text: * aviveko nijākhyātir māyā mohas tadātmakaḥ || SivSV_1.9:3 ||
body.translated_text: * Non-discrimination is one's own non-recognition; <s>Māyā</s> is delusion consisting of that;

body.text: * sauṣuptaṃ yoginām etat tritayaṃ dhāraṇādikam || SivSV_1.9:4 ||
body.translated_text: * this triad of deep sleep, for <s>yogins</s>, corresponds to <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) and the others.
* In the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s>, waking and the rest are also described:
* In the void, having the nature of the absence of intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) etc., in the state of I-ness and agency,
* when there are only unclear impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) without form, there is emptiness of knowable objects;

body.text: * sākṣāṇām āntarī vṛttiḥ prāṇādiprerikā matā || SivSV_1.9:8 ||
body.translated_text: * the inner activity of the senses, considered as that which impels <s>prāṇa</s> etc.,
* or the I-consciousness called the vital force (<s>jīvana</s>) in <s>prāṇa</s>, having the nature of the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>) —

body.text: * tāvan mātrasthitau proktaṃ sauṣuptaṃ pralayopamam || SivSV_1.9:10 ||
body.translated_text: * as long as one remains in mere (limited awareness), it is called deep sleep, resembling dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>),
* with or without objects of knowledge, with or without <s>māyā</s>-impurity.
* Even on the path of mind alone, through confusion due to being objects of the senses,

body.text: * spaṣṭāvabhāsā bhāvānāṃ sṛṣṭiḥ svapnapadaṃ matam || SivSV_1.9:13 ||
body.translated_text: * the vivid manifestation of entities, the creation (of objects), is considered the state of dreaming.

body.text: * sarvākṣagocaratvena yā tu bāhyatayā sthirā || SivSV_1.9:14 ||
body.translated_text: * But that which is stable externally through being the object of all senses,

body.text: * sṛṣṭiḥ sādhāraṇī sarvapramātṇāṃ sa jāgaraḥ || SivSV_1.9:15 ||
body.translated_text: * the creation common to all subjects — that is waking.
* Thus, having stated in detail, following worldly and yogic (perspectives),
* in this triad of waking etc., for one who is vigilantly awake,
* through union with the circle of powers (<s>śakticakra</s>), which is the cause of the dissolution of the universe,
* the recognition of non-difference pervaded by the experience of the fourth state (<s>turya</s>), which removes non-recognition,

body.text: * sphuraty avirataṃ yasya sa taddhārādhirohataḥ || SivSV_1.9:20 ||
body.translated_text: * flashes forth unceasingly for that one; he, ascending that stream,
* the <s>yogin</s>, pervaded by the state beyond the fourth (<s>turyātīta</s>), touching the proclaimed consciousness.]
The enjoyer of the triad (of states) is the Lord of Heroes (<s>Vīreśa</s>). // SivS 1.10 //

children.translated_text: * The triad of waking etc., through the stated union with the circle of powers (<s>śakticakra</s>),

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]
* sprinkled with the essence of the bliss of the fourth state (<s>turyānanda</s>), through abandonment of difference,
* contemplating the supreme space (<s>paramaṃ vyoma</s>) immersed in the flavor of bliss,

body.text: * tritayasyāsya yo bhoktā camatkartā sa yogirāṭ || SivSV_1.10:4 ||
body.translated_text: * he who is the enjoyer of this triad, the wonderer (<s>camatkartā</s>), is the king of <s>yogins</s>.

body.text: * triṣu dhāmasu yad bhogyaṃ bhoktā yaś ca prakīrtitaḥ || SivSV_1.10:5 ||
body.translated_text: * In the three abodes, what is to be enjoyed and who the enjoyer is — both are proclaimed;

body.text: * vidyāt tad ubhayaṃ yas tu sa bhuñjāno na lipyate || SivSV_1.10:6 ||
body.translated_text: * he who knows both of these, though enjoying, is not stained.
* Thus, possessing the splendor of the sovereignty of unopposed awareness as described,
* a mass of consciousness (<s>cidghana</s>), filled with the supreme bliss of self-knowledge,
* he is <s>Vīreśa</s> (Lord of Heroes), because of the heroes (powers) that devour differentiation,
* he is the supreme lord of the senses that move inward and outward.
* Are there stages that indicate his ascent to and repose in the supreme consciousness-reality?

body.text: * bhūmikāḥ santy ayaṃ yābhir yāti sarvottarāṃ sthitim || SivSV_1.10:12 ||
body.translated_text: * Are there stages through which he attains the highest state?
* To pacify this doubt in the student's heart, it is declared that there are:]
Wonder (<s>vismaya</s>) is the stages of <s>yoga</s>. // SivS 1.11 //

children.text: * yathā sātiśayānande kasyacid vismayo bhavet || SivSV_1.11:1 ||
children.translated_text: * Just as in extraordinary bliss, wonder arises for someone,

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]
* so too for this <s>yogin</s>, constantly, in the perception of each and every object of knowledge,
* when the senses are stilled by the experience of incomparable supreme bliss,

body.text: * pare svātmany atṛptyaiva yad āścaryaṃ sa vismayaḥ || SivSV_1.11:4 ||
body.translated_text: * the very insatiability in the supreme Self — that wonder is this (yogic) amazement (<s>vismaya</s>).

body.text: * sa eva khalu yogasya paratattvaikyarūpiṇaḥ || SivSV_1.11:5 ||
body.translated_text: * That indeed is of <s>yoga</s>, whose nature is oneness with the supreme reality (<s>paratattva</s>),
* the stages, indicating progressive ascent and repose in the supreme.
* For one whose consciousness has ascended the stages of <s>yoga</s> marked by such wonder,]
The will-power (<s>icchāśakti</s>) is <s>Umā</s>, the virgin (<s>Kumārī</s>). // SivS 1.12 //

children.translated_text: * For one who has attained the eternal state of supreme <s>Bhairava</s> through yogic practice,

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]

body.text: * tasyaiva yogino yecchā śaktiḥ saiva bhavaty umā || SivSV_1.12:2 ||
body.translated_text: * that very will-power (<s>icchāśakti</s>) of the <s>yogin</s> becomes <s>Umā</s> herself;

body.text: * parā bhaṭṭārikā saiva kumārīti prakīrtitā || SivSV_1.12:3 ||
body.translated_text: * that supreme Goddess (<s>parā Bhaṭṭārikā</s>) is proclaimed as <s>Kumārī</s> (the virgin).
* Through the play (<s>līlā</s>) of universal creation etc. from <s>Sadāśiva</s> down to earth,

body.text: * kumārī kuṃ mahāmāyābhūmiṃ mārayatīty api || SivSV_1.12:5 ||
body.translated_text: * <s>Kumārī</s> is so called because she slays (<s>mārayati</s>) the ground (<s>ku</s>) of <s>Mahāmāyā</s>.
* And <s>Kumārī</s> is the one to be enjoyed by this <s>yogin</s> who is of the nature of <s>Bhairava</s>;

body.text: * kumārī nānyabhogyā ca bhoktraikātmyena tiṣṭhati || SivSV_1.12:7 ||
body.translated_text: * <s>Kumārī</s> is not to be enjoyed by another; she abides in oneness with the enjoyer.
* <s>Umā</s>, the <s>Kumārī</s>, having abandoned all attachment, devoted to the Great Lord (<s>Maheśa</s>),

body.text: * ārādhanaparā tadvad icchā śaktis tu yoginaḥ || SivSV_1.12:9 ||
body.translated_text: * is intent on worship — similarly is the will-power (<s>icchāśakti</s>) of the <s>yogin</s>.

body.text: * ayam eva sphuṭaḥ pāṭho dṛṣṭo 'nuttaradaiśikaiḥ || SivSV_1.12:10 ||
body.translated_text: * This very clear reading has been seen by the teachers of the <s>Anuttara</s> (unsurpassed) tradition.]

body.text: * vyākhyātaś ca paraiḥ śaktitametipaṭhanāt punaḥ || SivSV_1.12:11 ||
body.translated_text: And it has been explained by others; moreover, from the reading '<s>śaktitama</s>' (most powerful), (SivSV 1.12:11)
the excellence of that <s>śakti</s> (power) has been expounded in terms of knowledge and action. (SivSV 1.12:12)
Thus, for the <s>yogī</s> endowed with the power of will (<s>icchāśakti</s>) of such potency, (SivSV 1.12:13)
The visible [universe] is the body. (SivS 1.13)

children.text: * yad yad dṛśyam aśeṣaṃ tac charīraṃ tasya yoginaḥ || SivSV_1.13:1 ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is visible, all of that without exception is the body of that <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 1.13:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * aham ity apṛthaktvena pativat pratibhāsanāt || SivSV_1.13:2 ||
body.translated_text: because it shines as 'I' in non-difference, just as [the body shines] for the Lord. (SivSV 1.13:2)
The body — [encompassing] the physical body, intellect, vital breath, and the void — like a pot and so forth, (SivSV 1.13:3)

body.text: * dṛśyam evāsya paśuvat draṣṭṛtvena na bhāsate || SivSV_1.13:4 ||
body.translated_text: is merely visible for him; like a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), it does not shine as the seer. (SivSV 1.13:4)

body.text: * evaṃ dehe ca bāhye ca sarvatraivāsya yoginaḥ || SivSV_1.13:5 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, in the body and in the external [world], everywhere for this <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 1.13:5)
by the analogy of the pigment within a peacock's egg, there arises non-dual cognition. (SivSV 1.13:6)

body.text: * dṛśyaṃ śarīratām eti śarīraṃ cāpi dṛśyatām || SivSV_1.13:7 ||
body.translated_text: The visible becomes the body, and the body also becomes the visible, (SivSV 1.13:7)

body.text: * ity uktaṃ yogino yat tan na durghaṭam itīryate || SivSV_1.13:8 ||
body.translated_text: this is what has been stated regarding the <s>yogī</s>; it is said that this is not difficult to accomplish. (SivSV 1.13:8)
In the heart, through the contact of consciousness (<s>citta</s>), there is the perception of the sleep-nature of the visible, (SivSV 1.13:9)

body.text: * hṛdayaṃ tad vijānīyād viśvasyāyatanaṃ mahat || SivSV_1.13:10 ||
body.translated_text: one should know that heart as the great abode of the universe. (SivSV 1.13:10)
By the stated principle, the heart is the ground and foundation of the repose of the universe, (SivSV 1.13:11)

body.text: * svasaṃvit tatra saṃghaṭṭaś cittasya calataḥ sataḥ || SivSV_1.13:12 ||
body.translated_text: self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvit</s>) is there; the contact is of the mind which exists in motion, (SivSV 1.13:12)
the nature of being alert through the apprehension of identity with that. (SivSV 1.13:13)
Therefore, of the visible universe, which takes the form of blue, body, and so forth, (SivSV 1.13:14)
there is also the perception of its sleep-nature, its absence, and even of the void. (SivSV 1.13:15)

body.text: * svāṅgarūpeṣu bhāveṣu pramātā kathyate patiḥ || SivSV_1.13:16 ||
body.translated_text: The cognizer (<s>pramātā</s>) is called the Lord in respect to entities that are of the nature of his own limbs, (SivSV 1.13:16)

body.text: * iti śrīpratyabhijñoktanītyā patyur iva prabhoḥ || SivSV_1.13:17 ||
body.translated_text: thus, by the principle stated in the revered <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>, just as for the Lord, the master, (SivSV 1.13:17)
there is the manifestation of that as his own limbs, as it truly is. (SivSV 1.13:18)

body.text: * ukte 'py evaṃ prameye 'sminn upāyāntaram ucyate || SivSV_1.13:19 ||]
body.translated_text: Even though this object of knowledge has been thus stated, another means is now described. (SivSV 1.13:19)
Or, from contemplation of the pure principle, the power of the unbound. (SivS 1.14)

children.text: * śuddhaṃ tattvaṃ paraṃ vastu yat tat paraśivātmakam || SivSV_1.14:1 ||
children.translated_text: The pure principle (<s>śuddha tattva</s>) is the supreme reality, which is of the nature of <s>Paraśiva</s>, (SivSV 1.14:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
its contemplation (<s>saṃdhāna</s>) is the meditation on the manifold world as being of that nature, (SivSV 1.14:2)

body.text: * tenaiva yasya paśvākhyā bandhaśaktir na vidyate || SivSV_1.14:3 ||
body.translated_text: by that very [contemplation], for whom the binding power called '<s>paśu</s>' (bound soul) does not exist, (SivSV 1.14:3)

body.text: * tat sadāśivavatso 'pi viśvasya jagataḥ patiḥ || SivSV_1.14:4 ||
body.translated_text: he, like <s>Sadāśiva</s>, though [still embodied], is the lord of the entire universe, (SivSV 1.14:4)
for this <s>yogī</s> who possesses the contemplation of the pure principle. (SivSV 1.14:5)
Deliberation (<s>vitarka</s>) is self-knowledge. (SivS 1.15)

children.translated_text: For the <s>yogī</s> whose bondage has been destroyed by the previously stated contemplation, <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation) is (SivSV 1.15:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * viśvātmā śiva evāham asmīty arthavicintanam || SivSV_1.15:2 ||
body.translated_text: the reflection on the meaning 'I am indeed <s>Śiva</s>, the Self of the universe,' (SivSV 1.15:2)

body.text: * etad eva sphuradrūpam ātmano jñānam ucyate || SivSV_1.15:3 ||
body.translated_text: this very [reflection], whose nature is radiant, is called knowledge of the Self. (SivSV 1.15:3)
Moreover, for this one who possesses the stated self-knowledge born of deliberation, (SivSV 1.15:4)
The bliss of the world is the joy of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption). (SivS 1.16)

children.text: * lokyaṃ lokayitā ceti lokaś cetyacidātmani || SivSV_1.16:1 ||
children.translated_text: The perceivable, the perceiver, and consciousness — this is '<s>loka</s>' (world) in the non-conscious [realm], (SivSV 1.16:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * tattadrūpatayā tasmiṃ loke sphurati yoginaḥ || SivSV_1.16:2 ||
body.translated_text: in that world, in the form of each respective [entity], there shines forth for the <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 1.16:2)
the consciousness of object and subject is common to all embodied beings, (SivSV 1.16:3)

body.text: * yogināṃ tu viśeṣo 'yaṃ sambandhe sāvadhānatā || SivSV_1.16:4 ||
body.translated_text: but the distinction for <s>yogīs</s> is this: attentiveness in the relation [between subject and object], (SivSV 1.16:4)

body.text: * ity uktanītyā tat sarvam aham ity anusaṃhiteḥ || SivSV_1.16:5 ||
body.translated_text: by the stated principle, from the synthesis of all that as 'I,' (SivSV 1.16:5)

body.text: * ānando yo bhavaty antas tat samādhisukhaṃ smṛtam || SivSV_1.16:6 ||
body.translated_text: the bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) that arises within is known as the joy of <s>samādhi</s>. (SivSV 1.16:6)

body.text: * yat samādhisukhaṃ tasya svātmārāmasya yoginaḥ || SivSV_1.16:7 ||
body.translated_text: That which is the joy of <s>samādhi</s> of that <s>yogī</s> who delights in the Self, (SivSV 1.16:7)

body.text: * tad eva loke lokānām ānando 'ntarvicinvatām || SivSV_1.16:8 ||
body.translated_text: that itself is the bliss of the world for worldly beings who reflect within. (SivSV 1.16:8)

body.text: * vibhūtiyogam etasya darśayaty atha yoginaḥ || SivSV_1.16:9 ||]
body.translated_text: Now it is shown the practice of supernatural powers (<s>vibhūti</s>) of this <s>yogī</s>. (SivSV 1.16:9)
By contemplation of <s>Śakti</s> (power), the creation of bodies [at will]. (SivS 1.17)

children.text: * icchā śaktir umety ādisūtroktā śaktir asya yā || SivSV_1.17:1 ||
children.translated_text: The power of will (<s>icchā śakti</s>), which is <s>Umā</s>, as stated in the earlier sūtra — that <s>śakti</s> which belongs to him, (SivSV 1.17:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * saṃdhāne yoginas tasyās tanmayībhāvane sati || SivSV_1.17:2 ||
body.translated_text: when the <s>yogī</s> contemplates it, when he becomes one with it, (SivSV 1.17:2)
by its power, the creation of bodies fit for the respective desires is established, (SivSV 1.17:3)

body.text: * anyāś ca siddhayas tasya sambhavantīty udīryate || SivSV_1.17:4 ||]
body.translated_text: and other supernatural accomplishments (<s>siddhis</s>) also arise for him — thus it is declared. (SivSV 1.17:4)
Union with elements, separation of elements, and uniting of the entire universe. (SivS 1.18)

children.translated_text: Of the elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) — body, intellect, vital breath, and void — which are of the nature of the cognizer, (SivSV 1.18:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * grāhyāṇāṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ ca saṃdhānaṃ paripoṣaṇam || SivSV_1.18:2 ||
body.translated_text: and of the cognizable, such as immovable [entities], <s>saṃdhāna</s> (union) means nourishment and integration, (SivSV 1.18:2)
separation (<s>pṛthaktva</s>) means dissociation for the pacification of afflictions such as disease, (SivSV 1.18:3)
and of the universe, which is distant in space, time, and so forth, (SivSV 1.18:4)
<s>saṃghaṭṭa</s> (uniting) means making directly perceptible through the eye and other senses, and so forth, (SivSV 1.18:5)

body.text: * etat sarvaṃ bhavec chaktisaṃdhāne sati yoginaḥ || SivSV_1.18:6 ||
body.translated_text: all of this occurs for the <s>yogī</s> when contemplation of <s>Śakti</s> takes place, (SivSV 1.18:6)

body.text: * yadā parimitāḥ siddhīr anicchan punar icchati || SivSV_1.18:7 ||
body.translated_text: when, not desiring limited accomplishments, he again desires (SivSV 1.18:7)

body.text: * viśvātmatāprathārūpāṃ parāṃ siddhiṃ tadāsya tu || SivSV_1.18:8 ||]
body.translated_text: the supreme accomplishment, which is of the nature of the manifestation of universal selfhood — then for him, (SivSV 1.18:8)
From the rise of pure knowledge (<s>śuddhavidyā</s>), the attainment of lordship over the collective [of powers]. (SivS 1.19)

children.translated_text: When the <s>yogī</s>, desiring the manifestation of universal selfhood, contemplates his own <s>śakti</s>, (SivSV 1.19:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * yadā yogī tadā tasya sadāśivapadaspṛśaḥ || SivSV_1.19:2 ||
body.translated_text: then, for him who has touched the state of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, (SivSV 1.19:2)

body.text: * īśvaro bahir unmeṣo nimeṣo 'ntaḥ sadāśivaḥ || SivSV_1.19:3 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Īśvara</s> is the outward opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>), and <s>Sadāśiva</s> is the inward closing (<s>nimeṣa</s>), (SivSV 1.19:3)
and there is co-referentiality of the 'I'-cognition and 'this'-cognition in <s>Sadvidyā</s> (pure knowledge), (SivSV 1.19:4)

body.text: * iti nītyā jagat sarvam aham eveti yā matiḥ || SivSV_1.19:5 ||
body.translated_text: by this principle, the cognition 'I alone am the entire universe' — (SivSV 1.19:5)

body.text: * sā śuddhā nirmalā vidyā tadīyād udayāt sphuṭam || SivSV_1.19:6 ||
body.translated_text: that is the pure, stainless <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge); from its arising, clearly, (SivSV 1.19:6)

body.text: * unmajjanāt sa cicchaktim ātmano nityam āmṛśet || SivSV_1.19:7 ||
body.translated_text: from its emergence, he would constantly apprehend the <s>cit-śakti</s> (power of consciousness) of the Self, (SivSV 1.19:7)

body.text: * yadā yogī tadā tasya cakreśatvam anuttaram || SivSV_1.19:8 ||
body.translated_text: when the <s>yogī</s> [does so], then his lordship over the collective (<s>cakreśatva</s>) is unsurpassed, (SivSV 1.19:8)
the sovereignty of <s>Maheśvara</s> is accomplished through the excellence of <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption) for the <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 1.19:9)
he who is both of the nature of the universal Self and transcendent, delighting in the Self, (SivSV 1.19:10)

body.text: * icchati svacchacidrūpo yadā yogī tadāsya tu || SivSV_1.19:11 ||]
body.translated_text: when the <s>yogī</s>, whose consciousness is transparent, wills it — then for him, (SivSV 1.19:11)
From contemplation of the great lake (<s>mahāhrada</s>), the experience of the power of <s>mantras</s>. (SivS 1.20)

children.translated_text: The supreme goddess (<s>parā bhaṭṭārikā</s>), consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>), preceded by the power of will (<s>icchāśakti</s>), (SivSV 1.20:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
emitting the entire inner universe up to gross knowable objects, (SivSV 1.20:2)
of the cognizer — the inner and outer forms, the senses, and objects, (SivSV 1.20:3)
of the streams of <s>Khecarī</s> and other [energies], which have both external and internal forms, (SivSV 1.20:4)
being the impeller [of all these], due to the qualities of transparency, depth, and so forth, (SivSV 1.20:5)
[she is] the great lake (<s>mahāhrada</s>), pervading the universe, beyond space, time, and so forth, (SivSV 1.20:6)
from the inner contemplation of that, from the apprehension of identity [with it], (SivSV 1.20:7)
of the mass of sounds (<s>śabdarāśi</s>) whose nature is the manifestation from the letter 'a' to the letter 'kṣa,' (SivSV 1.20:8)
which causes agitation within the principles (<s>tattvas</s>) from earth to <s>Śiva</s>, (SivSV 1.20:9)
of <s>mantravīrya</s> (the power of mantra) which is the life-force of all <s>mantras</s>, (SivSV 1.20:10)
which consists in the apprehension of the supreme I-consciousness — there is clear experience. (SivSV 1.20:11)

body.text: * akhilaṃ vācakaṃ vācyam aham ity avamarśanam || SivSV_1.20:12 ||
body.translated_text: The apprehension of the entire signifier and signified as 'I' — (SivSV 1.20:12)

body.text: * yoginaḥ sāvadhānasya bhavatīty eva śiṣyate || SivSV_1.20:13 ||
body.translated_text: this arises for the <s>yogī</s> who is attentive — thus it is taught. (SivSV 1.20:13)

body.text: * sphuṭīkaromi saṃkṣepāt tat prameyaṃ puroditam || SivSV_1.20:14 ||
body.translated_text: I shall briefly clarify that object of knowledge stated above. (SivSV 1.20:14)

body.text: * mahāhrada iti proktā śaktir bhagavatī parā || SivSV_1.20:15 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>mahāhrada</s> (great lake) refers to the supreme divine <s>Śakti</s>, (SivSV 1.20:15)
'contemplation' (<s>anusaṃdhāna</s>) refers to the reflective awareness of identity with that, (SivSV 1.20:16)
'<s>mantravīrya</s>' (power of mantra) refers to the reflective awareness of the full I-consciousness, (SivSV 1.20:17)

body.text: * tadīyo 'nubhavas tasya sphuraṇaṃ svātmanaḥ sphuṭam || SivSV_1.20:18 ||
body.translated_text: its 'experience' (<s>anubhava</s>) is the clear radiance of one's own Self. (SivSV 1.20:18)
Thus, devoted to illuminating the <s>Śāmbhavopāya</s> (the means of <s>Śiva</s>), (SivSV 1.20:19)
the first awakening (<s>unmeṣa</s>), properly characterized by the unfolding of one's own nature, [is complete]. (SivSV 1.20:20)

children.translated_text: The mind (<s>citta</s>) is <s>mantra</s>. (SivS 2.1)

body.translated_text: <s>Śivasūtra</s>, Second Awakening (<s>Dvitīya Unmeṣa</s>)

children.translated_text: By which the supreme Self-principle is known and reflected upon — (SivSV 2.1:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
this is <s>citta</s> (mind): the reflective awareness of the radiant Self's grace and so forth, (SivSV 2.1:2)

body.text: * tad eva mantryate guptam abhedena vimṛśyate || SivSV_2.1:3 ||
body.translated_text: that very [mind] is 'mantried' — the hidden [reality] is reflected upon in non-duality, (SivSV 2.1:3)

body.text: * svasvarūpam aneneti mantras tenāsya daiśikaiḥ || SivSV_2.1:4 ||
body.translated_text: one's own true nature [is reflected upon] by this — therefore it is <s>mantra</s>, as explained by the teachers, (SivSV 2.1:4)
the quality of spontaneous resonance and pulsation through contemplation of the full I-consciousness, (SivSV 2.1:5)
and the quality of protection (<s>trāṇa</s>) through the destruction of <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is declared. (SivSV 2.1:6)
Through the apprehension of the <s>mantra</s>'s deity, having attained equality with that, (SivSV 2.1:7)

body.text: * ārādhakasya cittaṃ ca mantras taddharmayogataḥ || SivSV_2.1:8 ||
body.translated_text: the mind of the worshiper also becomes <s>mantra</s> through union with its qualities. (SivSV 2.1:8)
And of this stated <s>mantra</s>, whose nature is contemplation (<s>manana</s>) and protection (<s>trāṇa</s>), (SivSV 2.1:9)
Effort (<s>prayatna</s>) is the accomplisher. (SivS 2.2)

children.translated_text: Having the nature of the agent that arises from the steadfast contemplation of the stated <s>mantra</s>, (SivSV 2.2:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * prayatno 'ntaḥsvasaṃrambhaḥ sa eva khalu sādhakaḥ || SivSV_2.2:2 ||
body.translated_text: effort is the inner self-exertion; that indeed is the accomplisher (<s>sādhaka</s>), (SivSV 2.2:2)
because it is said to bestow unity between the <s>mantra</s>-reciter and the <s>mantra</s>-deity. (SivSV 2.2:3)
Of the <s>mantra</s>, which has such an accomplisher and such a goal, the previously stated (SivSV 2.2:4)

body.text: * vīryaṃ vistarataḥ samyag varṇyate 'tha salakṣaṇam || SivSV_2.2:5 ||]
body.translated_text: power (<s>vīrya</s>) is now properly described in detail, along with its characteristics. (SivSV 2.2:5)
The being of the body of knowledge is the secret of <s>mantra</s>. (SivS 2.3)

children.translated_text: <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge) is that whose nature is the realization of the supreme non-duality, (SivSV 2.3:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * śarīraṃ yasya bhagavān śabdarāśiḥ sa ucyate || SivSV_2.3:2 ||
body.translated_text: he whose body is the blessed aggregate of words (<s>śabdarāśi</s>) — he is spoken of, (SivSV 2.3:2)
his being (<s>sattā</s>) is of the nature of the full I-consciousness pervading all pathways (<s>adhvans</s>), (SivSV 2.3:3)
that very radiance is [the essence] of <s>mantras</s> whose nature is contemplation and protection, (SivSV 2.3:4)

body.text: * guptārthatāyā jananaṃ rahasyam iti kathyate || SivSV_2.3:5 ||
body.translated_text: the generation of hidden meaning is called the secret (<s>rahasya</s>). (SivSV 2.3:5)
This has been extracted from the <s>Tantrasāra</s> by the revered <s>Kṣemarāja</s>, (SivSV 2.3:6)
and properly described through concordant, authoritative [passages] proceeding in their own commentarial manner. (SivSV 2.3:7)

body.text: * samyag evaṃvidhaṃ mantravīryaṃ yeṣāṃ yathātatham || SivSV_2.3:8 ||
body.translated_text: For those for whom such <s>mantravīrya</s> (power of mantra), properly and as it truly is, (SivSV 2.3:8)
has been conveyed through the method of contemplation of the <s>mahāhrada</s> (great lake), and yet (SivSV 2.3:9)
by the will of the great Lord (<s>Maheśa</s>) alone, does not firmly enter the heart, (SivSV 2.3:10)

body.text: * na gacchaty atha tucchāyāṃ cittaṃ siddhau prarohati || SivSV_2.3:11 ||
body.translated_text: their mind then sprouts into a trifling accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>), (SivSV 2.3:11)
arising from <s>bindu</s>, <s>nāda</s>, and so forth — for those <s>yogīs</s> of limited [attainment]. (SivSV 2.3:12)
In the womb [of ignorance], the expansion of mind is the dream of undifferentiated knowledge. (SivS 2.4)

children.translated_text: The womb (<s>garbha</s>) is ignorance (<s>akhyāti</s>), the great illusion (<s>Mahāmāyā</s>); in the accumulation of accomplishments of that nature, (SivSV 2.4:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * vikāso nāma cittasya tāvanmātre kṛtārthatā || SivSV_2.4:2 ||
body.translated_text: the expansion of mind means being satisfied with just that much, (SivSV 2.4:2)
that itself is undifferentiated knowledge (<s>aviśiṣṭā vidyā</s>), whose nature is partial knowing, (SivSV 2.4:3)
impure knowledge — that is the dream, filled with <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual constructions), (SivSV 2.4:4)

body.text: * āgatā api tāḥ siddhīḥ khalīkṛtya yadā punaḥ || SivSV_2.4:5 ||
body.translated_text: but when, having set aside even those accomplishments that have come, (SivSV 2.4:5)

body.text: * avaṣṭabhnāty asau yogī parāṃ siddhiṃ tadāśnute || SivSV_2.4:6 ||]
body.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> firmly persists, then he attains the supreme accomplishment. (SivSV 2.4:6)
Upon the natural arising of [pure] knowledge, the state of <s>Śiva</s> is <s>Khecarī</s> (the one who moves in the space of consciousness). (SivS 2.5)

children.translated_text: Of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), whose form was previously described, by the will of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, (SivSV 2.5:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
upon its natural arising — its spontaneous efflorescence, born of its own nature, (SivSV 2.5:2)
upon its emergence, [the yogī] being intent on immersion beyond trifling accomplishments, (SivSV 2.5:3)
the state which is non-different from the inner state of <s>Śiva</s>, (SivSV 2.5:4)
that very radiance, whose nature is the overflowing of perfect self-bliss, (SivSV 2.5:5)

body.text: * mudaṃ rātīty ato mudrā khecarī ca nabhaścarī || SivSV_2.5:6 ||
body.translated_text: gives (<s>rāti</s>) joy (<s>mud</s>) — therefore it is called <s>mudrā</s>; and <s>Khecarī</s> means 'moving in the sky [of consciousness],' (SivSV 2.5:6)
it is manifest everywhere for the <s>yogī</s> whose nature transcends the universe. (SivSV 2.5:7)
Thus, for the attainment of the power of <s>mantra</s> and <s>mudrā</s> of such potency, (SivSV 2.5:8)
The <s>guru</s> is the means. (SivS 2.6)

children.translated_text: The proper establishment of right knowledge, action, breath, <s>mantra</s>, and <s>mudrā</s> — (SivSV 2.6:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * gṛṇāty upadiśaty arthaṃ tadvīryaṃ cety ato guruḥ || SivSV_2.6:2 ||
body.translated_text: He [the guru] speaks, teaches the meaning, and [reveals] its power — therefore [he is called] <s>Guru</s>. || SivSV 2.6:2 ||
He alone, through revealing the pervasion of the power of <s>mantras</s> and <s>mudrās</s>, || SivSV 2.6:3 ||

body.text: * upāyaḥ kathyate sākṣād upeyaṃ paramaṃ prati || SivSV_2.6:4 ||
body.translated_text: Is described as the direct means toward the supreme goal. || SivSV 2.6:4 ||

body.text: * yad vā guruḥ parā śaktir īśvarānugrahātmikā || SivSV_2.6:5 ||
body.translated_text: Or, the <s>Guru</s> is the supreme <s>Śakti</s> (power), whose nature is the grace of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord). || SivSV 2.6:5 ||
By granting opportunity, she herself becomes the means. || SivSV 2.6:6 ||

body.text: * sa gurur matsamaḥ prokto mantravīryaprakāśakaḥ || SivSV_2.6:7 ||
body.translated_text: That <s>Guru</s>, equal to me [<s>Śiva</s>], is declared to be the revealer of the power of <s>mantras</s>. || SivSV 2.6:7 ||

body.text: * ādimāntyavihīnās tu mantrāḥ syuḥ śaradabhravat || SivSV_2.6:8 ||
body.translated_text: But <s>mantras</s> without beginning and end are like autumn clouds [i.e., powerless]. || SivSV 2.6:8 ||

body.text: * guror lakṣaṇam etāvad ādimāntyaṃ ca vedayet || SivSV_2.6:9 ||
body.translated_text: The mark of the <s>Guru</s> is precisely this — that he makes known the beginning and end [of mantras]. || SivSV 2.6:9 ||
Thus, by the authority stated in the sacred <s>Mālinīśāstra</s> and <s>Siddhatantra</s>, || SivSV 2.6:10 ||
From the spontaneous self-awareness of 'I' (<s>aham-āmarśa</s>) which knows the beginning and end, || SivSV 2.6:11 ||
From that <s>Guru</s>, who is equal to <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (the Supreme Lord), [who is] the supreme means. || SivSV 2.6:12 ||
<s>Mātṛkā-cakra-saṃbodhaḥ</s> (Awakening to the wheel of the Mother-letters) // SivS 2.7 //

children.translated_text: For the practitioner whose mind is continuously engaged in the contemplation of <s>mantras</s> and <s>mudrās</s>, || SivSV 2.7:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * bhavaty uktaguroḥ prītāt sādhakasyeti śiṣyate || SivSV_2.7:2 ||
body.translated_text: From the aforementioned pleased <s>Guru</s>, this is taught: || SivSV 2.7:2 ||

body.text: * athādyās tithayaḥ sarve svarā bindvavasānagāḥ || SivSV_2.7:3 ||
body.translated_text: Now, the initial <s>tithis</s> (lunar phases) — all the vowels ending in <s>bindu</s> (dot) and <s>visarga</s> (aspiration) — || SivSV 2.7:3 ||
Within them, by the conjunction of time, <s>Soma</s> (moon) and <s>Sūrya</s> (sun) are proclaimed. || SivSV 2.7:4 ||
The <s>tattvas</s> (principles) from earth onward up to <s>Puruṣa</s>, in the five || SivSV 2.7:5 ||

body.text: * kramāt kādiṣu vargeṣu makārānteṣu suvrate || SivSV_2.7:6 ||
body.translated_text: Consonant groups beginning with 'ka' and ending with 'ma', in order, O virtuous one. || SivSV 2.7:6 ||
The four <s>dhāraṇās</s> (concentrations) of wind, fire, water, and <s>Indra</s> (earth), || SivSV 2.7:7 ||

body.text: * tadūrdhve śādi vikhyātaṃ purastād brahmapañcakam || SivSV_2.7:8 ||
body.translated_text: Above those, beginning with 'śa', is proclaimed the fivefold <s>Brahma</s> group. || SivSV 2.7:8 ||

body.text: * amūlā tatkramāj jñeyā kṣāntā sṛṣṭir udāhṛtā || SivSV_2.7:9 ||
body.translated_text: Beginning from 'a', one should know the emission [of creation] ending with 'kṣa', in that order. || SivSV 2.7:9 ||

body.text: * sarveṣāṃ caiva mantrāṇāṃ vidyānāṃ ca yaśasvini || SivSV_2.7:10 ||
body.translated_text: Of all <s>mantras</s> and <s>vidyās</s> (sacred knowledge), O glorious one, || SivSV 2.7:10 ||

body.text: * iyaṃ yoniḥ samākhyātā sarvatantreṣu sarvadā || SivSV_2.7:11 ||
body.translated_text: This [<s>Mātṛkā</s>] is declared to be the source (<s>yoni</s>) always, in all <s>tantras</s>. || SivSV 2.7:11 ||
Thus, by the method taught in the sacred <s>Trīśikāśāstra</s> (<s>Parātrīśikā</s>), the <s>Mātṛkā</s> || SivSV 2.7:12 ||
Contains within it the sixteen vowels from 'a' to <s>visarga</s>. || SivSV 2.7:13 ||
Therefore, in the order of the fifteen <s>tithis</s> beginning with <s>bindu</s> and ending with <s>bindu</s>, || SivSV 2.7:14 ||
Adorned by the pair of <s>bindus</s> that are its essence and that transcend it. || SivSV 2.7:15 ||

body.text: * ata eva jagat sarvaṃ sṛjaty antar anuttare || SivSV_2.7:16 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore it creates the entire universe internally, in the unsurpassable [consciousness]. || SivSV 2.7:16 ||
Then, by the five vowels extracted from the end of the fifteenfold [system], || SivSV 2.7:17 ||

body.text: * a i u ṛ ḷ vinyāsaiḥ kādimāntaṃ ca vācakam || SivSV_2.7:18 ||
body.translated_text: By the arrangements of a, i, u, ṛ, ḷ — the designating [letters] from 'ka' to 'ma', || SivSV 2.7:18 ||
And the designated collection of <s>tattvas</s> from earth to <s>Puruṣa</s>, || SivSV 2.7:19 ||
Manifested in five groups of five, diversified in fivefold [manner], || SivSV 2.7:20 ||

body.text: * bahiś cānuttarād eva sṛjatī viśvam īdṛśam || SivSV_2.7:21 ||
body.translated_text: She externally creates the universe in this manner from the unsurpassable [consciousness] itself. || SivSV 2.7:21 ||

body.text: * vāyvagnisalilendrāṇāṃ kramād ya ra la vātmanām || SivSV_2.7:22 ||
body.translated_text: Of wind, fire, water, and <s>Indra</s> — in order, having the nature of ya, ra, la, va, || SivSV 2.7:22 ||
From the mutual conjunction of the triad called <s>Anuttara</s> (supreme), <s>Icchā</s> (will), and <s>Unmeṣa</s> (opening), || SivSV 2.7:23 ||
Moreover, by the conjunction of the pair called <s>Anuttara</s> and <s>Ṣaṇḍha</s> (neuter/androgynous), || SivSV 2.7:24 ||
Of those [tattvas] that have arisen — designated as <s>Kalā</s>, <s>Vidyā</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, and <s>Rāga</s>, || SivSV 2.7:25 ||
Through concealment of [the self's] true nature and removal of omnipotence and other [divine powers], || SivSV 2.7:26 ||
Bestowing limited agency and other [limited capacities] upon the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) who has been fragmented, || SivSV 2.7:27 ||
Through the obstruction of ascending to the <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> above <s>Māyā</s>, || SivSV 2.7:28 ||

body.text: * mūlād adho 'varohasya nirodhāc ca triśaṇkuvat || SivSV_2.7:29 ||
body.translated_text: And through the obstruction of descending below the root — like <s>Triśaṅku</s> [suspended in mid-air], || SivSV 2.7:29 ||
Of that [soul] established in the middle, through the holding by those of the nature of <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), || SivSV 2.7:30 ||
The regularity that governs the arising of the states of being and non-being [of things], || SivSV 2.7:31 ||

body.text: * kālo 'pi tāṃ mahāmāyāṃ svatantrām anuvartate || SivSV_2.7:32 ||
body.translated_text: Even <s>Kāla</s> (time) follows that great <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, which is autonomous. || SivSV 2.7:32 ||
By this statement, since they [the six tattvas] are bound by time and regularity, being sixfold in nature, || SivSV 2.7:33 ||

body.text: * sphārayantī vapuḥ paścāt tadūrdhvaṃ śādipañcakam || SivSV_2.7:34 ||
body.translated_text: Expanding the form, thereafter above that the five [letters] beginning with 'śa', || SivSV 2.7:34 ||
The body of <s>Brahma</s> extending from <s>Sadyojāta</s> to <s>Īśāna</s>, || SivSV 2.7:35 ||
Consisting of earth, water, fire, wind, and space in subtle form, || SivSV 2.7:36 ||
Having the nature of <s>Śuddhavidyā</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Śiva</s> in sequence, || SivSV 2.7:37 ||
Expanding what is within through the creative power of <s>visarga</s> (emission) externally, || SivSV 2.7:38 ||
Since the letter 'kṣa', though last, resides within the letters from 'ka' to 'sa', || SivSV 2.7:39 ||
Therefore, by [the letters] 'a' and 'ha', [forming] '<s>aham</s>' (I), without separation, || SivSV 2.7:40 ||
Having embraced the manifest world by <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, it shines forth. || SivSV 2.7:41 ||

body.text: * asyās tv evaṃprabhāvāyāś cakraṃ yat tad ihoditam || SivSV_2.7:42 ||
body.translated_text: Of this [<s>Mātṛkā</s>] of such power, what is called its 'wheel' (<s>cakra</s>) is here stated: || SivSV 2.7:42 ||
The cluster of vibrating powers (<s>spanda-śakti</s>) beginning with <s>Anuttara</s>, <s>Icchā</s>, <s>Unmeṣa</s>, etc. || SivSV 2.7:43 ||
Awakening to that [wheel] is the self-gathering into one's own self which is a mass of consciousness and bliss (<s>cidānanda</s>). || SivSV 2.7:44 ||
Now, for one whose self has been awakened by such awakening to the <s>Mātṛkā-cakra</s>, || SivSV 2.7:45 ||
<s>Śarīraṃ haviḥ</s> (The body is the oblation) // SivS 2.8 //

children.text: * śūnyaṃ dhīḥ prāṇa ity etat sṛjyate kṣīyate 'pi ca || SivSV_2.8:1 ||
children.translated_text: Void, intellect, <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) — these are created and also destroyed; || SivSV 2.8:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * sthairyam asti paraṃ dehāpekṣayā na tu tattvataḥ || SivSV_2.8:2 ||
body.translated_text: Their stability is merely relative to the body, not in reality. || SivSV 2.8:2 ||

body.text: * ity uktanītyā śūnyādeḥ pramātā tv asya bhittibhūḥ || SivSV_2.8:3 ||
body.translated_text: By the stated principle, the knower (<s>pramātā</s>) is the ground-basis of [entities beginning with] the void. || SivSV 2.8:3 ||
The body — gross, subtle, etc. — of the supreme <s>yogī</s>, || SivSV 2.8:4 ||
When offered into the fire of consciousness, is called the oblation (<s>havis</s>), because of the submersion of its subjecthood in that [fire], || SivSV 2.8:5 ||
Which grants the emergence of the knower whose nature is fully perfect illumination. || SivSV 2.8:6 ||
Thus, with the body as oblation, the flames of awakening blaze upward. || SivSV 2.8:7 ||
<s>Jñānam annam</s> (Knowledge is food) // SivS 2.9 //

children.text: * jñānaṃ bandha iti proktaṃ yat prāk tat parayoginaḥ || SivSV_2.9:1 ||
children.translated_text: That which was previously stated as 'knowledge is bondage' — for the supreme <s>yogī</s>, || SivSV 2.9:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * anātmany ātmatājñaptir annaṃ grasyata ity ataḥ || SivSV_2.9:2 ||
body.translated_text: The false cognition of self in what is not-self — that is the 'food' which is consumed; therefore, || SivSV 2.9:2 ||

body.text: * kiṃ ca yad yat prakāśātmasvarūpāmarśanātmakam || SivSV_2.9:3 ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, whatever knowledge has the nature of reflective awareness (<s>āmarśana</s>) of the luminous self, || SivSV 2.9:3 ||
That knowledge is called 'food' because it brings supreme delight. || SivSV 2.9:4 ||

body.text: * yadā tv avahitaḥ śaśvad yogī naivaṃ bhavaty asau || SivSV_2.9:5 ||
body.translated_text: But when the <s>yogī</s> is constantly attentive, he does not become thus [bound]; || SivSV 2.9:5 ||
Then, even for the one possessing knowledge, through the pride of [maintaining] <s>samādhāna</s> (absorption), || SivSV 2.9:6 ||
<s>Vidyā-saṃhāre tadutthasvapna-darśanam</s> (Upon the dissolution of <s>vidyā</s>, dream-vision arises) // SivS 2.10 //

children.text: * vidyeti jñānavisphārarūpā yā tu puroditā || SivSV_2.10:1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vidyā</s> means that [awareness] whose nature is the expansion of knowledge, as previously stated; || SivSV 2.10:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
That is <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (pure knowledge); upon its dissolution, when it does not arise, upon its submersion, || SivSV 2.10:2 ||
Of the dream born from that gradual dissolution of <s>vidyā</s>, || SivSV 2.10:3 ||
The vision of [that] dream which consists of the mass of <s>vikalpas</s> (conceptual constructs) grounded in differentiation, || SivSV 2.10:4 ||
The emergence occurs for this [practitioner] of the previously described supreme nature, || SivSV 2.10:5 ||
For the practitioner who is heedful in his attention — thus it is taught. || SivSV 2.10:6 ||
Thus [ends] the second <s>Unmeṣa</s> (Awakening), which illuminates <s>Śāktopāya</s> (the means through <s>Śakti</s>). || SivSV 2.10:7 ||

children.translated_text: <s>Ātmā cittam</s> (The self is the mind) // SivS 3.1 //

body.translated_text: <s>Śivasūtra</s>, Third <s>Unmeṣa</s> (Awakening)

children.translated_text: Formed by the entry of impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) of particular objects of experience such as sound, etc., || SivSV 3.1:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Oriented toward the operations of determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) and other functions of the instruments [of cognition], || SivSV 3.1:2 ||
Supported by the modes of <s>sattva</s>, etc., consisting of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), and <s>manas</s> (mind) — || SivSV 3.1:3 ||
That is <s>citta</s> (mind), because of the non-recognition of the previously stated nature of <s>caitanya</s> (consciousness). || SivSV 3.1:4 ||
Following the course of its various <s>karmas</s>, it wanders through different wombs [of birth]; || SivSV 3.1:5 ||

body.text: * atatīty ata evātmā tataḥ so 'ṇuḥ prakīrtitaḥ || SivSV_3.1:6 ||
body.translated_text: It 'wanders' (<s>atatī</s>), and therefore it is the <s>Ātman</s> (self); hence it is called <s>aṇu</s> (limited individual). || SivSV 3.1:6 ||
But there is no wandering for the <s>Ātman</s> whose sole nature is consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>); || SivSV 3.1:7 ||

body.text: * ataś caitanyam ātmeti dhīkriyātmakam ātmanaḥ || SivSV_3.1:8 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore <s>caitanya</s> (consciousness) is the <s>Ātman</s> — the true form of the self consisting of knowledge and action. || SivSV 3.1:8 ||

body.text: * viśvasvabhāvabhūtaṃ tat tāttvikaṃ rūpam īritam || SivSV_3.1:9 ||
body.translated_text: That which has become the nature of the universe — that is declared as its true essential nature. || SivSV 3.1:9 ||
Now, from the contraction manifested by its own freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>), || SivSV 3.1:10 ||

body.text: * saṃkocād aṇutāyogāc cittam ātmeti lakṣitam || SivSV_3.1:11 ||
body.translated_text: Due to that contraction and the condition of limitation (<s>aṇutā</s>), the self is designated as <s>citta</s> (mind). || SivSV 3.1:11 ||
Thus there is no inconsistency between the earlier and later teachings. || SivSV 3.1:12 ||

body.text: * asya cittasvarūpasya dehāder ātmanas tv aṇoḥ || SivSV_3.1:13 ||]
body.translated_text: Of this [self] whose nature is <s>citta</s> — the <s>Ātman</s>, the limited being beginning with the body. || SivSV 3.1:13 ||
<s>Jñānaṃ bandhaḥ</s> (Knowledge is bondage) // SivS 3.2 //

children.translated_text: Internally, having the mode of determining experienceable [objects] such as pleasure, etc.; || SivSV 3.2:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Externally, oriented toward objects appropriate to it — blue, body, and other such things; || SivSV 3.2:2 ||
Having the nature of the appearance of difference — that knowledge is bondage for the limited self (<s>aṇu</s>). || SivSV 3.2:3 ||

body.text: * tatpāśitatvād evāsāv aṇuḥ saṃsarati dhruvam || SivSV_3.2:4 ||
body.translated_text: Because it is bound by that [differentiated knowledge], this <s>aṇu</s> certainly transmigrates. || SivSV 3.2:4 ||

body.text: * jñānaṃ prakāśakaṃ loke ātmā caiva prakāśakaḥ || SivSV_3.2:5 ||
body.translated_text: Knowledge is illuminating in the world, and the self too is illuminating; || SivSV 3.2:5 ||

body.text: * anayor apṛthagbhāvāj jñānī jñāne prakāśate || SivSV_3.2:6 ||
body.translated_text: Due to their non-separation, the knower shines in knowledge. || SivSV 3.2:6 ||

body.text: * ity uktanītyā jñānaṃ ca svasvarūpaprakāśakam || SivSV_3.2:7 ||
body.translated_text: By the stated principle, knowledge too illuminates its own nature, || SivSV 3.2:7 ||

body.text: * ātmavat tat kathaṃ tasya bandhakatvaprasaṅgitā || SivSV_3.2:8 ||
body.translated_text: Like the self — then how can there be the possibility of it being a binder? || SivSV 3.2:8 ||

body.text: * ity āśaṅkyāha yady evaṃ prasannāt parameśvarāt || SivSV_3.2:9 ||
body.translated_text: Anticipating this objection, [the author] says: if from the gracious Supreme Lord || SivSV 3.2:9 ||

body.text: * pratyabhijñā bhavaty eṣā tadā satyaṃ tvadīritam || SivSV_3.2:10 ||
body.translated_text: This recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) arises, then what you say is true; || SivSV 3.2:10 ||

body.text: * tanmāyāśaktito naiṣa vimarśo 'sya yadā tadā || SivSV_3.2:11 ||]
body.translated_text: But when this reflective awareness does not [arise] due to His <s>Māyā-śakti</s>, then [knowledge becomes bondage]. || SivSV 3.2:11 ||
<s>Kalādīnāṃ tattvānām aviveko māyā</s> (Non-discrimination of the <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>Kalā</s> is <s>Māyā</s>) // SivS 3.3 //

children.translated_text: Of the <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>Kalā</s> and extending to earth, which are the <s>kañcukas</s> (coverings), || SivSV 3.3:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Which internally manifest, bestowing limited agency and other [limited powers], || SivSV 3.3:2 ||
Existing in the form of the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body) and as the gross body, etc., || SivSV 3.3:3 ||
Non-discrimination of these — the identification with them as self — || SivSV 3.3:4 ||

body.text: * saiva sammohinī māyā tattvākhyātimayaṃ jagat || SivSV_3.3:5 ||
body.translated_text: That itself is the deluding <s>Māyā</s>; the world is [thus] pervaded by non-recognition of the <s>tattvas</s>. || SivSV 3.3:5 ||
Therefore, for this <s>yogī</s>, [the practice is aimed at] the pacification of this <s>Māyā</s> produced by [conditioned] beings. || SivSV 3.3:6 ||
<s>Śarīre saṃhāraḥ kalānām</s> (Dissolution of the <s>kalās</s> in the body) // SivS 3.4 //

children.translated_text: In the gross body consisting of the great elements, in the subtle body consisting of <s>puryaṣṭaka</s>, || SivSV 3.4:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * mūlādisamanānte ca śarīre yoginaḥ pare || SivSV_3.4:2 ||
body.translated_text: And in the supreme body [of the yogī] ending with <s>samanā</s> beginning from the <s>mūla</s> (root), || SivSV 3.4:2 ||

body.text: * kalānāṃ tatra bhāgānāṃ kāryāṇāṃ kāraṇe nije || SivSV_3.4:3 ||
body.translated_text: Of the <s>kalās</s> (parts) therein — of the effects in their own cause — || SivSV 3.4:3 ||
The dissolution is the establishing of the sole fire of consciousness, through the contemplation of absorption (<s>laya</s>), || SivSV 3.4:4 ||

body.text: * dāhādyāmarśayuktyā vā dhyātavya iti śiṣyate || SivSV_3.4:5 ||
body.translated_text: Or through the practice of reflective awareness such as burning, etc. — thus it is taught. || SivSV 3.4:5 ||

body.text: * evaṃ dhyānābhidhāno yaḥ saṃhāropāya īritaḥ || SivSV_3.4:6 ||
body.translated_text: Thus the means of dissolution called <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) has been stated. || SivSV 3.4:6 ||

body.text: * evam etat pradhānāṃś ca prāṇāyāmapuraḥsarān || SivSV_3.4:7 ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, he shows the other principal [means] preceded by <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), || SivSV 3.4:7 ||

body.text: * anyān samādhiparyantān upāyān darśayaty asau || SivSV_3.4:8 ||]
body.translated_text: And extending up to <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) — the other means. || SivSV 3.4:8 ||
<s>Nāḍī-saṃhāra-bhūtajaya-bhūtakaivalya-bhūtapṛthaktvāni</s> (Dissolution of the <s>nāḍīs</s>, conquest of the elements, isolation of the elements, and separation from the elements) // SivS 3.5 //

children.translated_text: These are to be contemplated by the diligent practitioner — thus it is taught. || SivSV 3.5:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
The dissolution of the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) carrying <s>prāṇa</s> and other [vital breaths] is through <s>prāṇa-saṃyama</s> (restraint of breath); || SivSV 3.5:2 ||
Through the sequential arising of <s>recaka</s> (exhalation) and other [phases], in the fire of <s>udāna</s> (ascending breath), || SivSV 3.5:3 ||
Bringing about dissolution in the central channel (<s>madhya-nāḍī</s>), through becoming one with it. || SivSV 3.5:4 ||

body.text: * bhūtānāṃ bhūjalādīnāṃ jayo yaḥ sa udīryate || SivSV_3.5:5 ||
body.translated_text: The conquest of the <s>bhūtas</s> (elements) — earth, water, etc. — is now described: || SivSV 3.5:5 ||
The <s>vāyavī dhāraṇā</s> (wind concentration) at the thumb; the <s>āgneyī</s> (fire concentration) at the center of the navel; || SivSV 3.5:6 ||

body.text: * māheyī kaṇṭhadeśe tu vāruṇī ghaṇṭikāśritā || SivSV_3.5:7 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>māheyī</s> (earth concentration) in the throat region; the <s>vāruṇī</s> (water concentration) at the uvula; || SivSV 3.5:7 ||
The <s>ākāśa-dhāraṇā</s> (space concentration) at the crown of the head — it is said to bestow all <s>siddhis</s> (attainments). || SivSV 3.5:8 ||
Thus, through the <s>dhāraṇās</s> taught in the <s>Svacchandaśāstra</s> (<s>Svacchanda Tantra</s>), [there is] mastery. || SivSV 3.5:9 ||

body.text: * bhūtebhyaḥ kila kaivalyaṃ cittapratyāhṛtis tataḥ || SivSV_3.5:10 ||
body.translated_text: Detachment from the elements (<s>bhūta-kaivalya</s>) is the withdrawal of the mind from them; || SivSV 3.5:10 ||
Separation (<s>pṛthaktva</s>) is the state of identity with one's own pure, untouched self. || SivSV 3.5:11 ||

body.text: * bhūtasaṃdhāna ityādisūtroktaṃ yat phalaṃ purā || SivSV_3.5:12 ||
body.translated_text: The fruit stated in the earlier <s>sūtra</s> beginning with 'union with the elements' (<s>bhūta-saṃdhāna</s>), || SivSV 3.5:12 ||
That is accomplished effortlessly by one endowed with <s>Śāmbhavopāya</s> (the means of <s>Śiva</s>); || SivSV 3.5:13 ||
But it is accomplished through effort by <s>Āṇavopāya</s> (the individual means) — this is the distinction. || SivSV 3.5:14 ||

body.text: * ity evaṃ dehaśuddhyādyaiḥ samādhyantaiś ca yā bhavet || SivSV_3.5:15 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, through purification of the body and other [practices] extending up to <s>samādhi</s>, whatever || SivSV 3.5:15 ||

body.text: * siddhiḥ sā mohavaraṇān nātmajñānād itīryate || SivSV_3.5:16 ||]
body.translated_text: <s>Siddhi</s> (attainment) arises — that is from the veil of delusion, not from self-knowledge — thus it is stated. || SivSV 3.5:16 ||
<s>Mohāvaraṇāt siddhiḥ</s> (Attainment [arises] from the veil of delusion) // SivS 3.6 //

children.text: * moho vimohinī māyā tatkṛtāvaraṇāt kila || SivSV_3.6:1 ||
children.translated_text: Delusion (<s>moha</s>) is the deluding <s>Māyā</s>; from the covering created by that, || SivSV 3.6:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Through the previously described method of <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) etc., attainment would be limited || SivSV_3.6:2 ||

body.text: * tattattattvopabhogātmā na tv asya paracitprathā || SivSV_3.6:3 ||
body.translated_text: [Such attainment] consists of the enjoyment of various <s>tattvas</s> (principles), but not the expansion of supreme consciousness || SivSV_3.6:3 ||
For one whose delusion has been destroyed, in <s>samādhi</s>, again at the forefront, || SivSV_3.6:4 ||
Resorting to the middle <s>prāṇa</s>, in the space between the paths of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, || SivSV_3.6:5 ||

body.text: * ālambya jñānaśaktiṃ ca tatsthaṃ caivāsanaṃ labhet || SivSV_3.6:6 ||
body.translated_text: And grasping the power of knowledge (<s>jñānaśakti</s>), one obtains the <s>āsana</s> (seat) established therein || SivSV_3.6:6 ||

body.text: * prāṇādisthūlabhāvaṃ tu tyaktvā sūkṣmam athāntaram || SivSV_3.6:7 ||
body.translated_text: Abandoning the gross nature of <s>prāṇa</s> etc., [one reaches] the subtle, then the inner; || SivSV_3.6:7 ||

body.text: * sūkṣmātītaṃ tu paramaṃ spandanaṃ labhyate yataḥ || SivSV_3.6:8 ||
body.translated_text: Since the supreme vibration (<s>spandana</s>) beyond the subtle is obtained, || SivSV_3.6:8 ||

body.text: * prāṇāyāmaḥ sa uddiṣṭo yasmān na cyavate punaḥ || SivSV_3.6:9 ||
body.translated_text: That is designated as <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), from which one does not fall again || SivSV_3.6:9 ||

body.text: * śabdādiguṇavṛttir yā cetasā hy anubhūyate || SivSV_3.6:10 ||
body.translated_text: The mental activity relating to qualities such as sound that is experienced by the mind, || SivSV_3.6:10 ||

body.text: * tyaktvā tāṃ paramaṃ dhāma praviśet tatsvacetasā || SivSV_3.6:11 ||
body.translated_text: Abandoning that, one should enter the supreme abode through one's own consciousness; || SivSV_3.6:11 ||
This is declared as <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal), the cutter of the bonds of worldly existence || SivSV_3.6:12 ||

body.text: * dhīguṇān samatikramya nirdhyeyaṃ cāvyayaṃ vibhum || SivSV_3.6:13 ||
body.translated_text: Transcending the qualities of the intellect, [one should meditate upon] that which is beyond meditation, imperishable, and all-pervading; || SivSV_3.6:13 ||

body.text: * dhyātvā dhyeyaṃ svasaṃvedyaṃ dhyānaṃ tac ca vidur budhāḥ || SivSV_3.6:14 ||
body.translated_text: Having meditated upon the object of meditation as self-experienced, the wise know that as <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) || SivSV_3.6:14 ||

body.text: * dhāraṇā paramātmatvaṃ dhāryate yena sarvadā || SivSV_3.6:15 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) is that by which the supreme Self-nature is held at all times; || SivSV_3.6:15 ||
That is designated as <s>dhāraṇā</s>, the destroyer of the bondage of worldly existence || SivSV_3.6:16 ||

body.text: * svaparastheṣu bhūteṣu jagaty asmin samānadhīḥ || SivSV_3.6:17 ||
body.translated_text: Having equal vision toward beings in one's own [body] and in others, in this world, || SivSV_3.6:17 ||

body.text: * śivo 'ham advitīyo 'haṃ samādhiḥ sa paraḥ smṛtaḥ || SivSV_3.6:18 ||
body.translated_text: "I am <s>Śiva</s>, I am non-dual" — that is remembered as the supreme <s>samādhi</s> || SivSV_3.6:18 ||
Thus, through the methods described by the lord of the <s>Mṛtyujit Tantra</s>, || SivSV_3.6:19 ||
Beginning with the control of breath and ending with <s>samādhi</s>, through the sequential stages, || SivSV_3.6:20 ||
Immersion in the supreme reality indeed takes place — so it is said || SivSV_3.6:21 ||]
Through conquest of delusion and infinite expansion, the attainment of innate knowledge (<s>sahajavidyā</s>) // SivS_3.7 //

children.text: * moho māyā nijākhyātis tajjayāt tatparābhavāt || SivSV_3.7:1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Moha</s> (delusion) is <s>māyā</s>, one's own non-recognition; through its conquest, through its destruction, || SivSV_3.7:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
The limitless [one] arisen through the sun of effort, [extending] to the limit of the cessation of impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>), || SivSV_3.7:2 ||

body.text: * ābhogo yasya vistāra īdṛśād darśitātmanaḥ || SivSV_3.7:3 ||
body.translated_text: Whose expansion (<s>ābhoga</s>) is the expanse — from such a one who has revealed the Self, || SivSV_3.7:3 ||

body.text: * bhavet sahajavidyāyā jayo lābho yoginaḥ || SivSV_3.7:4 ||
body.translated_text: The conquest, the attainment of innate knowledge (<s>sahajavidyā</s>), comes to the <s>yogin</s> || SivSV_3.7:4 ||
Thus, the great arising of pure knowledge (<s>śuddhavidyā</s>) obtained through the conquest of delusion || SivSV_3.7:5 ||]
Waking is the second ray // SivS_3.8 //

children.translated_text: Having thus enjoyed innate knowledge, through dependence on unity with that, || SivSV_3.8:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * jāgarūkaḥ sadā yogī jāgrad ity ayam ucyate || SivSV_3.8:2 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>yogin</s> who is ever wakeful — this is called "waking" || SivSV_3.8:2 ||
In relation to the I-consciousness (<s>svāhaṃtā</s>) that is the nature of perfect I-awareness (<s>ahaṃvimarśa</s>), the world || SivSV_3.8:3 ||

body.text: * dvitīyam idam ākāraṃ karo yasya svadīdhitiḥ || SivSV_3.8:4 ||
body.translated_text: Is this second form — [the yogin's] ray (<s>kara</s>) is his own radiance; || SivSV_3.8:4 ||
He becomes such, having made the world his own possession || SivSV_3.8:5 ||
Such is he, whose mind is always absorbed in self-awareness (<s>svātmavimarśa</s>) || SivSV_3.8:6 ||]
The Self is a dancer (<s>nartaka</s>) // SivS_3.9 //

children.translated_text: He dances, supported by his own essential nature concealed within, || SivSV_3.9:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
By his own will, on the canvas of his own consciousness, through the play of his own vibration; || SivSV_3.9:2 ||
Those various stages of his own — in the forms of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep — || SivSV_3.9:3 ||

body.text: * ābhāsayati yat tasmād ātmā nartaka ucyate || SivSV_3.9:4 ||
body.translated_text: Since he manifests [them], therefore the Self is called a dancer || SivSV_3.9:4 ||
For this <s>yogin</s> who is a dancer of such cosmic drama, || SivSV_3.9:5 ||
The world-teacher (<s>jagadguru</s>) declares the stage (<s>raṅga</s>) to be the place for assuming the roles || SivSV_3.9:6 ||]
The stage is the inner self (<s>antarātmā</s>) // SivS_3.10 //

children.translated_text: In this [inner self], one delights with a nature eager for the play of the cosmic drama; || SivSV_3.10:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Thus the stage is the inner self — the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) consisting of the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>) || SivSV_3.10:2 ||
The <s>yogin</s>, having established his footing there, through the play of his own sense-vibrations, || SivSV_3.10:3 ||
Should illuminate the cosmic drama extending from <s>Sadāśiva</s> to the earth || SivSV_3.10:4 ||
Of [the yogin] dancing on this stage that is the inner theater of the body, in his own inner self || SivSV_3.10:5 ||]
The senses are the spectators // SivS_3.11 //

children.translated_text: "The spectators" — the body that manifests the drama of worldly existence, || SivSV_3.11:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
The senses such as the eyes inwardly marvel at [the spectacle] of the <s>yogin</s> || SivSV_3.11:2 ||
Thus, for the <s>yogin</s> whose circle of senses has become spectators || SivSV_3.11:3 ||]
Through the mastery of the intellect (<s>dhī</s>), the attainment of <s>sattva</s> (pure being) // SivS_3.12 //

children.translated_text: <s>Dhī</s> (intellect) is the understanding skilled in the awareness of one's own true consciousness-nature; || SivSV_3.12:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Through its mastery alone, of <s>sattva</s> — the inner vibration (<s>spanda</s>), || SivSV_3.12:2 ||

body.text: * sphurattārūpiṇaḥ siddhir abhivyaktiḥ sphuṭaṃ bhavet || SivSV_3.12:3 ||
body.translated_text: The attainment, the clear manifestation of that which has the nature of luminous flashing, becomes evident || SivSV_3.12:3 ||
Thus, from the glory of attaining one's own luminous <s>sattva</s> || SivSV_3.12:4 ||]
The accomplished one has the state of freedom (<s>svatantrabhāva</s>) // SivS_3.13 //

children.text: * siddhaḥ sampanna evāsya bhavet paramayoginaḥ || SivSV_3.13:1 ||
children.translated_text: "Accomplished" (<s>siddha</s>) means fully realized — this is [the state] of the supreme <s>yogin</s>; || SivSV_3.13:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
The state of freedom is characterized by innate omniscience and omnipotence || SivSV_3.13:2 ||
The freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>) of the master is capable of bringing the entire universe under his control || SivSV_3.13:3 ||
The state of freedom alone is [the nature] of this one whose self is filled with his own bliss || SivSV_3.13:4 ||]
As [it is] there, so elsewhere // SivS_3.14 //

children.text: * yatra svābhāvike dehe sphuṭībhūtā svatantratā || SivSV_3.14:1 ||
children.translated_text: Where in one's natural body freedom (<s>svatantratā</s>) has become manifest, || SivSV_3.14:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * yathā tatra tathānyatra dehe bhavati yoginaḥ || SivSV_3.14:2 ||
body.translated_text: As [it is] there, so in another body it exists for the <s>yogin</s>; || SivSV_3.14:2 ||
[Freedom] whose nature is complete I-consciousness (<s>pūrṇāhaṃtā</s>) becomes manifest for the one who is united; || SivSV_3.14:3 ||

body.text: * na caivam apy udāsīnena bhāvyaṃ yogināpi tu || SivSV_3.14:4 ||]
body.translated_text: But even so, the <s>yogin</s> should not become indifferent || SivSV_3.14:4 ||]
Attention to the seed (<s>bījāvadhāna</s>) // SivS_3.15 //

children.text: * sphurattātmā parā śaktir bījaṃ viśvasya kāraṇam || SivSV_3.15:1 ||
children.translated_text: The supreme power (<s>parā śakti</s>), whose nature is luminous flashing, is the seed, the cause of the universe; || SivSV_3.15:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Attention to that is the repeated settling of the mind therein; || SivSV_3.15:2 ||

body.text: * yoginā sāvadhānena kartavyam iti śiṣyate || SivSV_3.15:3 ||
body.translated_text: It is taught that this should be done by the attentive <s>yogin</s> || SivSV_3.15:3 ||
Such a great <s>yogin</s>, attentive to the supreme power || SivSV_3.15:4 ||]
Seated [in that seat], he easily immerses in the lake // SivS_3.16 //

children.text: * āsyate sthīyate yasminn aikātmyeneti cāsanam || SivSV_3.16:1 ||
children.translated_text: That in which one sits and abides with oneness is the <s>āsana</s> (seat); || SivSV_3.16:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * śāktaṃ balaṃ yat tatrasthas tadevāntaḥ parāmṛśan || SivSV_3.16:2 ||
body.translated_text: Abiding there, inwardly contemplating that very <s>śākta</s> (power) force, || SivSV_3.16:2 ||
The <s>yogin</s>, freed from the exertion of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), etc., || SivSV_3.16:3 ||
In that which is the cause of the flowing forth of the great current [beginning with] <s>khecarī</s>, || SivSV_3.16:4 ||
In the lake endowed with qualities such as clarity and filled with his own bliss, || SivSV_3.16:5 ||
In the overflowing ocean of consciousness, complete, an island of objective reality, || SivSV_3.16:6 ||
Having abandoned all means, he immerses as he pleases || SivSV_3.16:7 ||
Through the very submersion of the body etc., he clearly becomes one with that || SivSV_3.16:8 ||
Thus, through the means obtained by <s>āṇavopāya</s> (individual means), from the conquest of delusion, || SivSV_3.16:9 ||
Through the excellence of the <s>śākta</s> immersion whose nature is the rising of pure knowledge, || SivSV_3.16:10 ||
Through the deep plunging into the lake of supreme bliss that has been made one's own, || SivSV_3.16:11 ||
The supreme practitioner [attains] the glory of the spontaneously flashing <s>śāmbhava</s> state || SivSV_3.16:12 ||]
He brings about the creation [of realities] by his own measure (<s>svamātrā</s>) // SivS_3.17 //

children.translated_text: The measure (<s>mātrā</s>) belonging to the self, of consciousness having the described form, || SivSV_3.17:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Is the contracted, measured portion characterized by the known and the knower; || SivSV_3.17:2 ||
The bringing about of its creation is the vision of it as [something] created; || SivSV_3.17:3 ||

body.text: * sampādayati yogīndro yatheṣṭaṃ spaṣṭam icchayā || SivSV_3.17:4 ||
body.translated_text: The lord of <s>yogins</s> accomplishes [this] as desired, clearly, by his will || SivSV_3.17:4 ||
Thus, for the <s>yogin</s> whose universal form arises from such power, || SivSV_3.17:5 ||

body.text: * punarjanmādisambandho na kaścid iti kathyate || SivSV_3.17:6 ||]
body.translated_text: There is no connection with rebirth etc. — so it is said || SivSV_3.17:6 ||]
Upon the imperishability of knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), there is destruction of birth // SivS_3.18 //

children.text: * vidyeti sahajā tasyā avināśaḥ sadodayaḥ || SivSV_3.18:1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge) means the innate [knowledge]; its imperishability is its constant arising; || SivSV_3.18:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
By that very [imperishability], of [the complex] accompanied by ignorance and connected with various <s>karmas</s>, || SivSV_3.18:2 ||
Of birth — the aggregate consisting of body, vital breath, intellect, etc., || SivSV_3.18:3 ||

body.text: * vināśo mūlavidhvaṃso bhavaty asyeti śiṣyate || SivSV_3.18:4 ||
body.translated_text: There is destruction, the annihilation from the root, of this [birth] — so it is taught || SivSV_3.18:4 ||

body.text: * yadā tu śuddhavidyāyāḥ svarūpaṃ tasya majjati || SivSV_3.18:5 ||
body.translated_text: But when the essential nature of pure knowledge (<s>śuddhavidyā</s>) submerges for him, || SivSV_3.18:5 ||
Then the powers arise precisely for his delusion || SivSV_3.18:6 ||]
In the <s>ka</s>-group etc. [of letters], <s>Māheśvarī</s> and the other [<s>śaktis</s>] are the mothers of the bound souls (<s>paśumātaraḥ</s>) // SivS_3.19 //

children.translated_text: Abiding in the <s>ka</s>-group etc. [of letters], having attained the status of presiders over them, || SivSV_3.19:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
<s>Māheśvarī</s> and the others, situated within the consciousness at the openings of the described senses, || SivSV_3.19:2 ||
[Deluding] the bound souls (<s>paśus</s>), from knowledge... ||
Entering the various grounds of cognition, || SivSV_3.19:3 ||
Through the penetration of those various sounds, through delusion, [they become] the mothers of the bound souls || SivSV_3.19:4 ||
Concealing one's own form, which is dense with consciousness and bliss, || SivSV_3.19:5 ||

body.text: * atimānaṃ vivṛṇvānāḥ śarīrādau jaḍe 'pi ca || SivSV_3.19:6 ||
body.translated_text: And revealing excessive identification with the body etc., even in the inert [matter], || SivSV_3.19:6 ||

body.text: * paśuvatsādhakam api pramattaṃ mohayanty amūḥ || SivSV_3.19:7 ||
body.translated_text: These [mothers] delude even the practitioner who is negligent, just as [they do] a bound soul || SivSV_3.19:7 ||

body.text: * tasmād bhāvyaṃ sadānena sāvadhānena yoginā || SivSV_3.19:8 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore the <s>yogin</s> should always be attentive; || SivSV_3.19:8 ||

body.text: * uktaṃ sāmānyato jñānādhiṣṭhānaṃ mātṛkety ataḥ || SivSV_3.19:9 ||
body.translated_text: It has been said generally that <s>mātṛkā</s> is the foundation of knowledge; || SivSV_3.19:9 ||

body.text: * idaṃ tu prāptatattvo 'pi pramādyan sādhakaḥ punaḥ || SivSV_3.19:10 ||
