body.translated_text: But here, even the practitioner who has attained the truth, if negligent again, || SivSV_3.19:10 ||

body.text: * paśvadhiṣṭhānabhūtābhir mohyate mātṛbhis tv iti || SivSV_3.19:11 ||
body.translated_text: Is deluded by the mothers who have become the basis for the bound state || SivSV_3.19:11 ||

body.text: * yata evam ataḥ śuddhavidyā prāptāpi yuktibhiḥ || SivSV_3.19:12 ||
body.translated_text: Since this is so, pure knowledge (<s>śuddhavidyā</s>), even though attained through methods, || SivSV_3.19:12 ||

body.text: * bahvībhiḥ sā punar mauḍhyādy athāsya na vinaśyati || SivSV_3.19:13 ||
body.translated_text: Through the many [śaktis], that [delusion] returns; yet for him, [the knowledge] does not permanently perish; || SivSV_3.19:13 ||

body.text: * tathā sarvāsv avasthāsu yukto bhūyād itīryate || SivSV_3.19:14 ||]
body.translated_text: Therefore, one should be united [with that knowledge] in all states — so it is declared || SivSV_3.19:14 ||]
The fourth [state] should be poured like oil into the three [states] // SivS_3.20 //

children.text: * triṣv iti proktarūpeṣu jāgarādiṣu tailavat || SivSV_3.20:1 ||
children.translated_text: "In the three" — in the stated forms of waking etc., like oil, || SivSV_3.20:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
"The fourth" — the previously described [state] whose nature is the expansion of pure knowledge, || SivSV_3.20:2 ||

body.text: * turyaṃ dhāma sadāsecyaṃ yathā syāt tanmayaṃ trayam || SivSV_3.20:3 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>turya</s> (fourth) state should always be poured so that the three [states] become permeated by it; || SivSV_3.20:3 ||

body.text: * yathā tailaṃ kramāt svīyam āśrayaṃ vyāpnuyāt tathā || SivSV_3.20:4 ||
body.translated_text: Just as oil gradually pervades its substrate, so [should the fourth pervade the three] || SivSV_3.20:4 ||
Through the flashing at the beginning and end points of waking etc., clearly, || SivSV_3.20:5 ||
One should moisten even the middle phase with the bliss-essence of <s>turya</s> || SivSV_3.20:6 ||
By the <s>sūtra</s> "waking..." etc., previously, through the quality of effort, || SivSV_3.20:7 ||
Of the supreme <s>yogin</s> who possesses the contemplation of the circle of powers (<s>śakticakra</s>), || SivSV_3.20:8 ||
In the stages of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep that flow forth spontaneously, || SivSV_3.20:9 ||
Was described the origination of the outflow of <s>turya</s> that emerges spontaneously || SivSV_3.20:10 ||
By the <s>sūtra</s> "the triad..." etc., through what is accomplished by <s>śāmbhavopāya</s> (Śiva's means), || SivSV_3.20:11 ||
The dissolution of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep through the process of forceful digestion (<s>haṭhapāka</s>) [was described]; || SivSV_3.20:12 ||
But by this <s>sūtra</s>, through the method of <s>āṇavopāya</s> (individual means), || SivSV_3.20:13 ||
The triad of stages beginning with waking, which remain like petals, || SivSV_3.20:14 ||
Should be sprinkled with the essence of <s>turya</s> — this distinction is declared || SivSV_3.20:15 ||
Here again, [the teacher] states the means for sprinkling with the nectar of <s>turya</s> || SivSV_3.20:16 ||]
Being immersed, one should enter with one's own consciousness // SivS_3.21 //

children.translated_text: Abandoning <s>prāṇāyāma</s> etc., the gross means that involve thought-constructs (<s>vikalpa</s>), || SivSV_3.21:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
With one's own consciousness, one's own awareness, in a thought-free (<s>avikalpa</s>) form, || SivSV_3.21:2 ||
Whose nature is the blissful wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) of inward-turned awareness, || SivSV_3.21:3 ||
Being immersed here in the essence of <s>turya</s>, the subjectivity of one's own body etc., || SivSV_3.21:4 ||

body.text: * majjanena praśamayan praviśet tat samāviśet || SivSV_3.21:5 ||
body.translated_text: Dissolving through immersion, one should enter, should merge with that || SivSV_3.21:5 ||
Thus, for one whose intellect is absorbed in the supreme state, from the very nature of reality, || SivSV_3.21:6 ||

body.text: * yadā bhūyaḥ prasaraṇaṃ yogino jāyate tadā || SivSV_3.21:7 ||]
body.translated_text: When there arises again an outflow for the <s>yogin</s>, then || SivSV_3.21:7 ||]
Equal vision in the movement of <s>prāṇa</s> // SivS_3.22 //

children.translated_text: Of <s>prāṇa</s> — [the yogin] refined by the absorption of the fragrance of the flashing <s>śākta</s> power, || SivSV_3.22:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Through the strength of the intellect that has fully opened and penetrated all the knots || SivSV_3.22:2 ||

body.text: * īṣad bahir mandamandaṃ cāre prasaraṇe sati || SivSV_3.22:3 ||
body.translated_text: When there is even a slight, very gentle outward movement of awareness, (SivSV 3.22:3)
equally, due to the nature of the bliss of consciousness (<s>cinmudghana</s>), there is always the perception of non-difference, (SivSV 3.22:4)

body.text: * saṃvedanaṃ bhavaty arthāt sarvāvasthāsu yoginaḥ || SivSV_3.22:5 ||
body.translated_text: this awareness naturally arises in all states for the <s>yogī</s>. (SivSV 3.22:5)
Through firm establishment in <s>turya</s> (the fourth state), <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth) is attainable, [though] one does not grasp it [directly]; (SivSV 3.22:6)
At the two junction points of the preceding and succeeding [states], when only <s>turya</s> is experienced, (SivSV 3.22:7)

body.text: * āste yogī tadāmuṣya tāvan mātreṇa tuṣyataḥ || SivSV_3.22:8 ||]
body.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> abides; then, being satisfied with just that measure [of <s>turya</s>]. (SivSV 3.22:8)
In the middle, [there is] an inferior creation. (SivS 3.23)

children.text: * pūrvasyām aparasyāṃ ca koṭau turyaniṣeviṇaḥ || SivSV_3.23:1 ||
children.translated_text: For one who cultivates <s>turya</s> (the fourth state) at the preceding and succeeding junction points, (SivSV 3.23:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
if that <s>yogī</s> becomes careless and heedless in attention, (SivSV 3.23:2)

body.text: * madhyāyām avaro 'śreṣṭhaḥ kutsitaḥ sarga āpatet || SivSV_3.23:3 ||
body.translated_text: in the middle [state], an inferior, unexcellent, contemptible creation may befall [him]; (SivSV 3.23:3)

body.text: * vyutthānātmā tato yogī sāvadhānaḥ sadā bhavet || SivSV_3.23:4 ||
body.translated_text: consisting of ordinary emergence (<s>vyutthāna</s>) — therefore the <s>yogī</s> should always be attentive. (SivSV 3.23:4)

body.text: * avaraprasave vṛtte hy evaṃ madhyapade punaḥ || SivSV_3.23:5 ||
body.translated_text: When inferior creation has occurred in this way in the middle state, again, (SivSV 3.23:5)
through relishing the firm establishment of <s>turya</s>, one should apprehend <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth). (SivSV 3.23:6)

body.text: mātrāsv apratyayasaṃdhāne naṣṭasya punar utthānam // SivS_3.24 //
body.translated_text: Upon the joining of thought-free awareness to the objects of experience (<s>mātrā</s>), there is the re-emergence of that [<s>turya</s> state] which had been lost. (SivS 3.24)

children.text: * mātrāḥ padārthāḥ rūpādyās tāsv ebhiś cakṣurādibhiḥ || SivSV_3.24:1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mātrā</s>s are the objects such as form and the like; in these, through the senses such as the eyes, (SivSV 3.24:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
the individual cognition (<s>svapratyaya</s>) is the awareness of each particular [sense's] own graspable [object]; (SivSV 3.24:2)

body.text: * saṃdhānaṃ tu samastaṃ tad aham ity anusaṃhitiḥ || SivSV_3.24:3 ||
body.translated_text: but the joining (<s>saṃdhāna</s>) is the synthesis 'all this is I' (<s>aham</s>); (SivSV 3.24:3)
when this [joining] occurs, for the one who was lost, driven away by the aforesaid group [of sense-objects], (SivSV 3.24:4)

body.text: * turyasya punar utthānaṃ bhūya unmajjanaṃ bhavet || SivSV_3.24:5 ||
body.translated_text: there is the re-emergence of <s>turya</s>, its rising up again. (SivSV 3.24:5)
Then the fullness that comes from the wealth of unity [with <s>turya</s>] is imparted to the supreme <s>yogī</s>. (SivSV 3.24:6)
Thus, the bull among practitioners (<s>sādhaka</s>s), with the intensity of awakening immersion (<s>samāveśa</s>), (SivSV 3.24:7)
Becomes equal to <s>Śiva</s>. (SivS 3.25)

children.translated_text: Through the excellence of the practice of <s>turya</s> (the fourth state), [having attained] the state whose nature is <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth), (SivSV 3.25:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
the practitioner, having directly attained [it], with the inner Self of all worlds, (SivSV 3.25:2)
with <s>Śiva</s>, who is of the nature of pure consciousness, transparent, free, and endowed with bliss, (SivSV 3.25:3)
becomes equal; and upon the dissolution of the body's limited aspects, [he becomes] <s>Śiva</s> [himself]. (SivSV 3.25:4)

body.text: * arjitaṃ dīkṣayā dagdhaṃ bhaviṣyanti yamādibhiḥ || SivSV_3.25:5 ||
body.translated_text: That [<s>karma</s>] which has been accumulated is burned by <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation); [the karmas] that would arise through <s>yama</s> (death) and the like, (SivSV 3.25:5)

body.text: * yenedaṃ sādhitaṃ yatra tadbhuktyā vinivartate || SivSV_3.25:6 ||
body.translated_text: that by which this [body] was brought about and in which [it operates] — that is exhausted through experience (<s>bhukti</s>). (SivSV 3.25:6)

body.text: * anekabhāvikaṃ karma dagdhaṃ bījam ivāgninā || SivSV_3.25:7 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>karma</s> that would produce many [future births] is burned like a seed by fire; (SivSV 3.25:7)

body.text: * bhaviṣyad api saṃruddhaṃ yenedaṃ tad dhi bhogataḥ || SivSV_3.25:8 ||
body.translated_text: even that which is yet to come is obstructed; that by which this [present life exists] is [consumed] through experience. (SivSV 3.25:8)
Thus, by the stated method, being the ground of experiencing the enjoyments that have arrived through <s>prārabdha</s> (commenced karma), (SivSV 3.25:9)
the maintenance of the body is taught as his duty. (SivSV 3.25:10)
The activity of the body is [his] <s>vrata</s> (vow). (SivS 3.26)

children.text: * evaṃ pūrvoktayā nītyā śivatulyasya yoginaḥ || SivSV_3.26:1 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the previously stated method, for the <s>yogī</s> who is equal to <s>Śiva</s>, (SivSV 3.26:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
whose self is ever devoted to the worship of his own Self whose nature is <s>Śiva</s>, (SivSV 3.26:2)
nourished by the nectar of pure, transparent devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) that shines forth from within, (SivSV 3.26:3)

body.text: * bhavatpūjopayogāya śarīram idam astu me || SivSV_3.26:4 ||
body.translated_text: 'May this body of mine serve the purpose of worshiping You' — (SivSV 3.26:4)
thus, in the direction stated by the illustrious, transcendent <s>Utpala</s> (<s>Utpaladeva</s>), (SivSV 3.26:5)

body.text: * śivabhaktisudhāpūrṇe śarīre vṛttir asya yā || SivSV_3.26:6 ||
body.translated_text: whatever activity there is in this body filled with the nectar of devotion to <s>Śiva</s>, (SivSV 3.26:6)

body.text: * vratam etad anuṣṭheyaṃ na tucchaṃ tasya dhāraṇam || SivSV_3.26:7 ||
body.translated_text: that is the <s>vrata</s> (vow) to be observed; its maintenance is not worthless. (SivSV 3.26:7)

body.text: * evaṃvidhasya tasyāsya yā yā svālāparūpiṇī || SivSV_3.26:8 ||]
body.translated_text: For one of such [nature], whatever conversation (<s>ālāpa</s>) naturally arises, (SivSV 3.26:8)
[His] conversation is <s>japa</s> (recitation). (SivS 3.27)

children.text: * mahāmantramayaṃ naumi rūpaṃ te svacchaśītalam || SivSV_3.27:1 ||
children.translated_text: 'I bow to Your form, which is made of the great <s>mantra</s>, transparent and cool, (SivSV 3.27:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
beautiful with unprecedented delight, and overflowing with the essence of supreme nectar' — (SivSV 3.27:2)
thus, in the direction taught by the author of the illustrious <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>, the [spiritual] guide, (SivSV 3.27:3)
for one who apprehends his own Self whose nature is the spontaneous I-awareness (<s>aham-āmarśa</s>), (SivSV 3.27:4)

body.text: * yā yā svairābhilāpātmā kathā yāthārthyavādinaḥ || SivSV_3.27:5 ||
body.translated_text: whatever spontaneous speech (<s>svairābhilāpa</s>) is the conversation of one who speaks the truth, (SivSV 3.27:5)

body.text: * bhūyobhūyaḥ pare bhāve bhāvanā bhāvyate hi yā || SivSV_3.27:6 ||
body.translated_text: the contemplation that is contemplated again and again upon the supreme reality, (SivSV 3.27:6)

body.text: * japaḥ so 'tra svayaṃ nādo mantrātmā japya īdṛśaḥ || SivSV_3.27:7 ||
body.translated_text: that is <s>japa</s> here; the spontaneous resonance (<s>nāda</s>) whose nature is <s>mantra</s> — such is the [true] recitation. (SivSV 3.27:7)
Twenty-one thousand six hundred [breaths] in a day and night — (SivSV 3.27:8)

body.text: * japo devyāḥ samuddiṣṭaḥ sulabho durlabho jaḍaiḥ || SivSV_3.27:9 ||
body.translated_text: this is the <s>japa</s> designated by the Goddess; easily accessible [to the wise], yet difficult to attain for the dull. (SivSV 3.27:9)
Thus, by the stated method, that [conversation], being the wealth of awareness of the Lord of the Self of all, (SivSV 3.27:10)
is called <s>japa</s> because its nature is generation and protection [of awareness]. (SivSV 3.27:11)
Moreover, whatever conversation concerns such a supreme <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 3.27:12)
that too is said to be <s>japa</s> for people, because it generates and protects [awareness]. (SivSV 3.27:13)
Now his conduct (<s>caryā</s>), which follows the [proper] boundaries, is described. (SivSV 3.27:14)
The gift (<s>dāna</s>) is self-knowledge. (SivS 3.28)

children.translated_text: The direct realization of the Self, whose nature is the previously described consciousness, (SivSV 3.28:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * yat taj jñānaṃ tad evāsya dānaṃ yatnena dīyate || SivSV_3.28:2 ||
body.translated_text: that is knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>); that itself is his gift (<s>dāna</s>), which is given with effort. (SivSV 3.28:2)

body.text: * paripūrṇaṃ svarūpaṃ svaṃ dīyate khaṇḍyate bhidā || SivSV_3.28:3 ||
body.translated_text: One's own complete nature is given; duality is shattered; (SivSV 3.28:3)

body.text: * dāyate śodhyate rūpam ātmīyaṃ dīyate punaḥ || SivSV_3.28:4 ||
body.translated_text: the self's form is purified, cleansed, and given again; (SivSV 3.28:4)
the <s>Śiva</s>-Self, recognized through <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition), is protected in its own essential nature; (SivSV 3.28:5)

body.text: * dīyate ceti yatnena svātmajñānam anuttaram || SivSV_3.28:6 ||
body.translated_text: and thus, the unsurpassed self-knowledge is given with effort. (SivSV 3.28:6)

body.text: * kṛpayā svātmaśiṣyebhyas tad anenaiva dīyate || SivSV_3.28:7 ||
body.translated_text: Out of compassion, that [knowledge] is given by this very [means] to his own disciples. (SivSV 3.28:7)

body.text: * evaṃ samyagvrataṃ proktaṃ japaṃ caryā ca pālayan || SivSV_3.28:8 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, properly observing the stated <s>vrata</s> (vow), <s>japa</s> (recitation), and <s>caryā</s> (conduct), (SivSV 3.28:8)
equal to <s>Śiva</s>, always devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s> as one's own Self, (SivSV 3.28:9)
this one alone is the great <s>yogī</s>, the bearer of the burden of the great <s>mantra</s>, (SivSV 3.28:10)
the one who truly awakens the essence (<s>tattva</s>) in the hearts of his resident disciples. (SivSV 3.28:11)

body.text: * ity āha bhagavān īśo nityānugrahakārakaḥ || SivSV_3.28:12 ||]
body.translated_text: Thus says the blessed Lord (<s>Īśa</s>), the eternal bestower of grace. (SivSV 3.28:12)
He who presides over the group [of powers] (<s>avipastha</s>) is the cause of knowledge. (SivS 3.29)

children.text: * avīn paśujanān pātīty avipaṃ śaktimaṇḍalam || SivSV_3.29:1 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Avi</s>' means the group of powers (<s>śaktimaṇḍala</s>) that protects the bound souls (<s>paśu</s>); (SivSV 3.29:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
it is said to be [the group] beginning with <s>Māheśvarī</s>, the presiding deities of the <s>ka</s>-group and other [phoneme groups]. (SivSV 3.29:2)

body.text: * adhitiṣṭhati yaḥ svairam avipasthaḥ sa ucyate || SivSV_3.29:3 ||
body.translated_text: He who freely presides [over them] is called <s>avipastha</s> (one who stands in the flock [of powers]). (SivSV 3.29:3)

body.text: * jānātīty akhilaṃ tat jñā jñānaśaktir udīryate || SivSV_3.29:4 ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Jñā</s>' [means] 'one who knows all' — thus the power of knowledge (<s>jñānaśakti</s>) is proclaimed; (SivSV 3.29:4)

body.text: * tasyā hetus tayā śiṣyān pratibodhayituṃ kṣamaḥ || SivSV_3.29:5 ||
body.translated_text: he is the cause of that [knowledge-power], able to awaken disciples through it. (SivSV 3.29:5)
But another, who has been made dependent by the circle of powers (<s>śakticakra</s>), (SivSV 3.29:6)

body.text: * svātmany evāsamarthaḥ san katham anyān prabodhayet || SivSV_3.29:7 ||
body.translated_text: being incapable even regarding his own Self — how could he awaken others? (SivSV 3.29:7)

body.text: * yac chabdāpekṣayā sūtre tac chabdo 'dhyāhṛtaḥ svayam || SivSV_3.29:8 ||
body.translated_text: That word which is expected in the <s>sūtra</s> has been itself supplied [by implication]; (SivSV 3.29:8)

body.text: * caśabdo hy arthavācy atra yasmāj jñānaprabodhane || SivSV_3.29:9 ||
body.translated_text: for the word '<s>ca</s>' here denotes a purpose: since in the awakening of knowledge, (SivSV 3.29:9)

body.text: * yogī hetus tato dānam ātmajñānam itīritam || SivSV_3.29:10 ||
body.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> is the cause — therefore 'the gift is self-knowledge' was stated. (SivSV 3.29:10)

body.text: * ity evam avipasthasya jñāhetor asya yoginaḥ || SivSV_3.29:11 ||]
body.translated_text: Thus, for this <s>yogī</s> who presides over the powers and is the cause of knowledge, (SivSV 3.29:11)
The universe is an expansion of his own powers. (SivS 3.30)

children.text: * śaktayo 'sya jagat kṛtsnaṃ śaktimāṃs tu maheśvaraḥ || SivSV_3.30:1 ||
children.translated_text: 'His powers are the entire universe, and the possessor of powers is the great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>)' — (SivSV 3.30:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * ity āgamadiśā viśvaṃ svaśaktipracayo yathā || SivSV_3.30:2 ||
body.translated_text: thus, according to the direction of the scriptures (<s>āgama</s>), just as the universe is an expansion of the powers of (SivSV 3.30:2)
<s>Śiva</s>, so too for this supreme <s>yogī</s> who is equal to Him, (SivSV 3.30:3)
of his own power (<s>śakti</s>), which is inseparable from his own Self and whose nature is awareness, (SivSV 3.30:4)

body.text: * pracayaḥ sphuraṇārūpo vikāso viśvam iṣyate || SivSV_3.30:5 ||
body.translated_text: the expansion, whose nature is vibrant manifestation (<s>sphuraṇa</s>), is considered to be the universe. (SivSV 3.30:5)

body.text: * na paraṃ sṛṣṭyavasthāyām amuṣya parayoginaḥ || SivSV_3.30:6 ||
body.translated_text: Not only in the state of creation for this supreme <s>yogī</s> (SivSV 3.30:6)
is the universe an expansion of his own powers, but also in the two [states] that follow it. (SivSV 3.30:7)
[Also in] maintenance and dissolution. (SivS 3.31)

children.text: * svaśaktipracayau proktau tāv apīty anuvartate || SivSV_3.31:1 ||
children.translated_text: They too are said to be expansions of one's own powers — thus '<s>svaśaktipracaya</s>' carries over [from the previous <s>sūtra</s>]. (SivSV 3.31:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Of the manifested universe, through one's own awareness, which is of the nature of action (<s>kriyā</s>), (SivSV 3.31:2)
with reference to each particular knower, for some time, in the mode of 'this-ness' (<s>idaṃtā</s>), (SivSV 3.31:3)

body.text: * yā sthitiś cinmayāhaṃtāviśrāntyātmā ca yo layaḥ || SivSV_3.31:4 ||
body.translated_text: that which is maintenance (<s>sthiti</s>), and that which is dissolution (<s>laya</s>) — the repose in the consciousness-nature of I-ness (<s>ahaṃtā</s>) — (SivSV 3.31:4)

body.text: * tāv ubhau yoginas tasya svaśaktipracayātmakau || SivSV_3.31:5 ||
body.translated_text: both of these, for that <s>yogī</s>, are of the nature of the expansion of his own powers. (SivSV 3.31:5)

body.text: * vikasat saṃkucat sarvaṃ vedyaṃ yat saṃvidātmakam || SivSV_3.31:6 ||
body.translated_text: All that is knowable, whether expanding or contracting, is of the nature of awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>), (SivSV 3.31:6)
since otherwise the cognition of that knowable [object] would be impossible. (SivSV 3.31:7)
But [objection:] since creation, maintenance, and destruction are mutually different, (SivSV 3.31:8)
has not the own essential nature of the <s>yogī</s> undergone change? (SivSV 3.31:9)

body.text: * ity āśaṅkānivṛttyarthaṃ sūtram āha maheśvaraḥ || SivSV_3.31:10 ||]
body.translated_text: To remove this doubt, the great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>) states the [next] <s>sūtra</s>. (SivSV 3.31:10)
Even during the occurrence of these [creation, etc.], there is no loss [of the <s>yogī</s>'s nature], because of [his] nature as the knower. (SivS 3.32)

children.text: * teṣāṃ sṛṣṭyādibhāvānāṃ pravṛttāv apy anāratam || SivSV_3.32:1 ||
children.translated_text: Even during the unceasing occurrence of those states beginning with creation, (SivSV 3.32:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
even during [their] emergence, for one endowed with unwavering yogic steadfastness, (SivSV 3.32:2)
there is a pair of states here, termed 'being an effect' and 'being an agent'; (SivSV 3.32:3)

body.text: * kāryatā kṣayiṇī tatra kartṛtvaṃ punar akṣayam || SivSV_3.32:4 ||
body.translated_text: the state of being an effect is perishable, but agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>) is imperishable. (SivSV 3.32:4)

body.text: * kāryonmukhaḥ prayatno yaḥ kevalaṃ so 'tra lupyate || SivSV_3.32:5 ||
body.translated_text: Only the effort directed toward [producing] an effect ceases here; (SivSV 3.32:5)

body.text: * tasmiṃl lupte vilupto 'smīty abudhaḥ pratipadyate || SivSV_3.32:6 ||
body.translated_text: when that ceases, the ignorant person concludes 'I am destroyed'; (SivSV 3.32:6)

body.text: * na tu yo 'ntarmukho bhāvaḥ sarvajñatvaguṇāspadam || SivSV_3.32:7 ||
body.translated_text: but the inward-turned being, which is the seat of the quality of omniscience, (SivSV 3.32:7)

body.text: * tasya lopaḥ kadācit syād anyasyānupalambhanāt || SivSV_3.32:8 ||
body.translated_text: can never be destroyed, since no other [agency] distinct from it is ever perceived. (SivSV 3.32:8)
Thus, according to the method stated in the illustrious <s>Spandaśāstra</s>, for this <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 3.32:9)
there is no loss — there is no falling away from his own nature as the knower (<s>saṃvettṛ</s>), (SivSV 3.32:10)
due to [his] nature as the perceiver, characterized by the wonder of the arising <s>turya</s> [state]; (SivSV 3.32:11)

body.text: * nirāse tasya sṛṣṭyādeḥ sṛjyasyāpy aprakāśanāt || SivSV_3.32:12 ||
body.translated_text: if the loss of creation and the like were to occur, even the created [universe] would not shine forth, (SivSV 3.32:12)
[but this is not the case,] for the <s>yogī</s> who is unshaken in the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the universe. (SivSV 3.32:13)
The contemplation of pleasure and pain is [merely] external. (SivS 3.33)

children.translated_text: For the wise one who has transcended the subjectivity of the body, <s>prāṇa</s>, and the like, (SivSV 3.33:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
who has conquered contact with objects, the contemplation of pleasure and pain (SivSV 3.33:2)
[occurs] externally, in the form of 'this-ness' (<s>idaṃtā</s>) appearances, like blue, yellow, and so forth; (SivSV 3.33:3)

body.text: * ahaṃ sukhīti duḥkhīti lokavan na tv ahaṃtayā || SivSV_3.33:4 ||
body.translated_text: not as 'I am happy' or 'I am suffering' in the mode of I-ness (<s>ahaṃtā</s>), as [it is] for worldly people, (SivSV 3.33:4)
because, according to the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> 'the universe is an expansion of one's own powers,' (SivSV 3.33:5)
everything shines forth for him as enveloped by I-ness (<s>ahaṃtā</s>). (SivSV 3.33:6)

body.text: * yogino laukikasyeva sukhādy eva na kevalam || SivSV_3.33:7 ||
body.translated_text: Not merely pleasure and the like, as for a worldly person, [is experienced by] the <s>yogī</s>; (SivSV 3.33:7)
one who has transcended the ego-sense (<s>ahaṃkṛti</s>) identified with body and the like, which is pervaded by the great delusion — (SivSV 3.33:8)
how could the king of <s>yogīs</s> be touched by pleasure and pain as a worldly person would be? (SivSV 3.33:9)
Due to the rising of the subjectivity of consciousness and the subsiding of the condition of the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>), (SivSV 3.33:10)

body.text: * yato na tatsukhādyantas tata evaiṣa sādhakaḥ || SivSV_3.33:11 ||]
body.translated_text: since he is not contained within pleasure and the like — for this very reason, this practitioner [is free]. (SivSV 3.33:11)
But one who is freed from that is <s>kevalī</s> (the isolated one). (SivS 3.34)

children.text: * tābhyāṃ mukto viśeṣeṇa yogīndro yat tayor yataḥ || SivSV_3.34:1 ||
children.translated_text: The supreme <s>yogī</s>, who is especially freed from those two [pleasure and pain], because from those, (SivSV 3.34:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * saṃskāreṇāpy asaṃspṛṣṭaḥ kevalī cinmayaḥ smṛtaḥ || SivSV_3.34:2 ||
body.translated_text: untouched even by their latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), is called <s>kevalī</s> (the isolated one), pure consciousness. (SivSV 3.34:2)
The word '<s>tu</s>' indicates a contrast with reference to what is about to be stated; (SivSV 3.34:3)
similarly, in the succeeding <s>sūtra</s>, with reference to this <s>sūtra</s>, (SivSV 3.34:4)

body.text: * tad evāha tuśabdoktam antaraṃ candraśekharaḥ || SivSV_3.34:5 ||]
body.translated_text: <s>Candraśekhara</s> (the moon-crested one, <s>Śiva</s>) states that very distinction indicated by the word '<s>tu</s>.' (SivSV 3.34:5)
But one who is conjoined with delusion (<s>moha</s>) is a <s>karmātman</s> (one whose nature is [bound] karma). (SivS 3.35)

children.text: * mohaḥ svākhyātir ajñānaṃ tena yaḥ pratisaṃhataḥ || SivSV_3.35:1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Moha</s> (delusion) is the failure of self-recognition, ignorance; one who is conjoined with that, (SivSV 3.35:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
having become solidly identified with it alone, thereby becomes the abode of suffering and the like. (SivSV 3.35:2)

body.text: * tata eva sa karmātmā śubhāśubhakalaṅkitaḥ || SivSV_3.35:3 ||
body.translated_text: For that very reason, he is a <s>karmātman</s> (karma-bound soul), tainted by merit and demerit; (SivSV 3.35:3)
but even for such a person, bound to various <s>karmas</s>, when (SivSV 3.35:4)
through the unobstructed descent of the power (<s>śaktipāta</s>) of the great Lord (<s>Maheśāna</s>), there begins to dawn (SivSV 3.35:5)

body.text: * svātantryayogaḥ sahajaḥ prādurasti tadāsya tu || SivSV_3.35:6 ||]
body.translated_text: the innate union with freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>), then it manifests for him. (SivSV 3.35:6)
When difference is concealed, there is the capacity for creating another creation. (SivS 3.36)

children.translated_text: Of difference (<s>bheda</s>), which arises from the limited I-consciousness of the body, vital breath, and so forth, (SivSV 3.36:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
whose nature is appropriate to the <s>sakala</s> and other [states], deluded and enveloped by <s>kalā</s> and other [limiting principles], (SivSV 3.36:2)
upon its concealment — the dispelling of that which persists, through the opening of one's own [awareness], (SivSV 3.36:3)
from the manifestation of one's own greatness through identity with <s>mantra</s> and lords of <s>mantras</s>, (SivSV 3.36:4)
there arises the capacity for creating another creation for this supreme <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 3.36:5)
the creatorship of fashioning whatever is desired clearly manifests. (SivSV 3.36:6)

body.text: * na caitad apy asaṃbhāvyaṃ sraṣṭṛtvaṃ yogino yataḥ || SivSV_3.36:7 ||]
body.translated_text: And this creatorship of the <s>yogī</s> is not impossible, because — (SivSV 3.36:7)
The power of the instruments [of perception] is [known] from one's own experience. (SivS 3.37)

children.translated_text: From oneself, from one's own experience, in dreams, imagination, and so forth, (SivSV 3.37:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
the making — the creation of one's own perceivable objects, subjects, and cognizables — (SivSV 3.37:2)
the power [behind] that creatorship, the unfolding of agency, is accomplished by self-awareness alone, (SivSV 3.37:3)

body.text: * sambhavantīṃ tathā sṛṣṭiṃ yadi dārḍhyena bhāvayet || SivSV_3.37:4 ||
body.translated_text: if one were to meditate with firmness on such a creation as actually occurring, (SivSV 3.37:4)
then there would arise a universal creation common to all. (SivSV 3.37:5)
Because the <s>karaṇaśakti</s> (power of the instruments) here is the power of absolute freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>), (SivSV 3.37:6)

body.text: * pramātur bodharūpasya sāraṃ tasmāt svamāyayā || SivSV_3.37:7 ||
body.translated_text: the essence of the cognizer whose nature is consciousness; therefore, toward the stimulation (SivSV 3.37:7)
of the power of freedom which has been concealed by one's own <s>māyā</s>, (SivSV 3.37:8)
The enlivening [of the three states] beginning with the three-fold [experience]. (SivS 3.38)

children.translated_text: The 'three-fold' (<s>tripada</s>) refers to waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, in sequence, (SivSV 3.38:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
each having beginning, middle, and end aspects, which are examined by indirect means, (SivSV 3.38:2)
having the nature of turning toward the object, absorption in it, and becoming one with it, (SivSV 3.38:3)
in the form of creation, maintenance, and dissolution — by <s>turya</s> (the fourth state) itself, beginning with that, (SivSV 3.38:4)
whose nature is the dense mass of the <s>rasa</s> (flavor) of wonder and bliss within that triad, (SivSV 3.38:5)
even though concealed by <s>māyā</s>, whose nature is obscuration, (SivSV 3.38:6)
flashing for a moment like lightning in the enjoyments of various objects, (SivSV 3.38:7)
the practitioner should perform the enlivening through attentiveness, (SivSV 3.38:8)
by that very life-force, he should properly stimulate (SivSV 3.38:9)

body.text: * samyaguttejanaṃ kuryād yenāsau tanmayo bhavet || SivSV_3.38:10 ||
body.translated_text: his own Self which is alive, so that he becomes one with that. (SivSV 3.38:10)

body.text: * turyānuprāṇanaṃ proktaṃ jāgarādau purā triṣu || SivSV_3.38:11 ||
body.translated_text: The enlivening of waking and other [states] by <s>turya</s> was stated previously in the three [states] (SivSV 3.38:11)
by the sūtra 'the fourth [should be poured like oil]' — by this [sūtra] 'three-fold' and so forth, (SivSV 3.38:12)
it is specified as being in the junctures of beginning, middle, and end of waking and other [states]. (SivSV 3.38:13)
Not only in the inward-facing state [of consciousness], (SivSV 3.38:14)

body.text: * tripadādiprāṇanam ity etad uktam athāpi tu || SivSV_3.38:15 ||]
body.translated_text: has it been said that there is enlivening beginning with the three-fold [experience], but also — (SivSV 3.38:15)
As in the establishment of the mind, [so also] in the body, the senses, and the external [world]. (SivS 3.39)

children.text: * anuprāṇanam ity etad ādadyād iti śiṣyate || SivSV_3.39:1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Should perform the enlivening' — this is what is taught; (SivSV 3.39:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
just as in the establishment of the mind in the inward-facing state, so also (SivSV 3.39:2)
with <s>turya</s> (the fourth state), whose nature is bliss, as stated for the enlivening, (SivSV 3.39:3)
one should do the same even in the outward-facing [state], in the body, senses, and objects, (SivSV 3.39:4)

body.text: * tanmayaṃ bhavatīty arthāt tadā sarvaṃ carācaram || SivSV_3.39:5 ||
body.translated_text: he becomes one with that — that is, everything movable and immovable [becomes that]. (SivSV 3.39:5)
Thus, for this one whose nature is self-bliss, the power characterized by absolute freedom (SivSV 3.39:6)
clearly becomes capable of creating entities as desired. (SivSV 3.39:7)

body.text: * yadā punar asau yogī proktāṃ turyātmikāṃ daśām || SivSV_3.39:8 ||
body.translated_text: But when this <s>yogī</s> does not apprehend inwardly the stated state which is of the nature of <s>turya</s>, (SivSV 3.39:8)

body.text: * āntarīṃ nāmṛśaty antas tadā dehādyahaṃkṛteḥ || SivSV_3.39:9 ||
body.translated_text: then, from the I-consciousness centered on the body and so forth, (SivSV 3.39:9)
which has the nature of feeling incomplete — this being the <s>āṇavamala</s> (innate impurity), (SivSV 3.39:10)
From craving, there is the outward movement of the one who is to be driven [through transmigration]. (SivS 3.40)

children.translated_text: By the <s>tattvas</s> (principles), occupied by hosts of powers, ending with earth, [and] by <s>kalā</s> and other [coverings], (SivSV 3.40:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * yoner yonyantaraṃ neyaḥ saṃvāhyaḥ paśur ucyate || SivSV_3.40:2 ||
body.translated_text: the one who is driven from womb to womb is called the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), (SivSV 3.40:2)
for him, due to the <s>āṇavamala</s> (innate impurity), following the respective <s>karmas</s>, (SivSV 3.40:3)
from craving, which is of the nature of feeling incomplete, there is outward movement, (SivSV 3.40:4)
the very turning toward objects — not the inner synthesis of principles. (SivSV 3.40:5)
But when, through the descent of the power (<s>śaktipāta</s>) of the great Lord (<s>Maheśāna</s>), there opens up (SivSV 3.40:6)

body.text: * ātmīyam eva vimṛśan nāste rūpaṃ tadāsya tu || SivSV_3.40:7 ||
body.translated_text: the reflection upon his own form alone — then for him (SivSV 3.40:7)

body.text: * abhāvād abhilāṣasya na bahirgatir āpatet || SivSV_3.40:8 ||
body.translated_text: from the absence of craving, there is no falling into outward movement, (SivSV 3.40:8)
but rather, as stated, there is the very delight in the Self — thus it is said. (SivSV 3.40:9)
For the one whose cognition has ascended to that, from the destruction of that [craving], there is the dissolution of the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>). (SivS 3.41)

children.translated_text: 'That' refers to the stated domain which has the nature of subjectivity — (SivSV 3.41:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
the cognition (<s>pramiti</s>) that has ascended [to it], the awareness devoted to reflecting upon it, (SivSV 3.41:2)

body.text: * yasya tasyāsya tad iti proktāṇavamalātmanaḥ || SivSV_3.41:3 ||
body.translated_text: for one who has that — then from the destruction of that which is said to be of the nature of <s>āṇavamala</s>, (SivSV 3.41:3)

body.text: * abhilāpasya rūḍhasya kṣayāj jīvasya saṃkṣayaḥ || SivSV_3.41:4 ||
body.translated_text: the craving that is established — from its destruction, there is the dissolution of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), (SivSV 3.41:4)
the pacification of that whose nature is the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body) truly occurs. (SivSV 3.41:5)

body.text: * prāpnoti dehapāto 'sya nanv evaṃ jīvasaṃkṣaye || SivSV_3.41:6 ||
body.translated_text: Does not the death of the body come about when the <s>jīva</s> is thus dissolved? (SivSV 3.41:6)

body.text: * nāsau kadāpi kasyāpi dṛśyate 'trāpi yoginaḥ || SivSV_3.41:7 ||
body.translated_text: Yet that is never seen for anyone — [not] even for the <s>yogī</s> in this case, (SivSV 3.41:7)

body.text: * tasmāt kathaṃ tadārūḍhapramitiḥ sādhako bhavet || SivSV_3.41:8 ||
body.translated_text: therefore, how can the one whose cognition has ascended to that become the practitioner? (SivSV 3.41:8)

body.text: * ity āśaṅkyottaraṃ vakti bhagavān viśvadaiśikaḥ || SivSV_3.41:9 ||]
body.translated_text: Anticipating this objection, the blessed universal teacher answers: (SivSV 3.41:9)

body.text: bhūtakañcukī tadā vimukto bhūyaḥ patisamaḥ paraḥ // SivS_3.42 //
body.translated_text: One whose covering is the elements — then, liberated, he is again equal to the Lord, supreme. (SivS 3.42)

children.translated_text: From the pacification of the stated craving, upon the dissolution of the <s>jīva</s>, (SivSV 3.42:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
even when the identification with the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>) as the cognizer dissolves, (SivSV 3.42:2)
with the elements that initiate the body not touching the I-principle, (SivSV 3.42:3)
he is especially liberated, as if merely wearing an armor of [elements] — by the fortune of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation), (SivSV 3.42:4)

body.text: * bhūyo bāhulyataḥ patyā samo 'yaṃ parameśinā || SivSV_3.42:5 ||
body.translated_text: again, abundantly, he is equal to the Lord, to <s>Parameśvara</s>, (SivSV 3.42:5)
his nature being the dense mass of consciousness and bliss, absorbed in the nature of That, (SivSV 3.42:6)

body.text: * tata eva paraḥ pūrṇaḥ samyak tanmayatāṃ gataḥ || SivSV_3.42:7 ||
body.translated_text: therefore he is supreme, complete, having properly become one with That. (SivSV 3.42:7)

body.text: * bhūtakañcukitāpy asya tadaiva na nivartate || SivSV_3.42:8 ||
body.translated_text: His being covered by elements does not cease even then — (SivSV 3.42:8)

body.text: * kasmād ity api śaṅkāyām uttaraṃ vakti śaṃkaraḥ || SivSV_3.42:9 ||]
body.translated_text: as to why, <s>Śaṃkara</s> states the answer to this doubt: (SivSV 3.42:9)
The connection with <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) is natural. (SivS 3.43)

children.text: * prāṇe pariṇatā saṃvit prāg iti proktayā diśā || SivSV_3.43:1 ||
children.translated_text: Consciousness that has transformed into <s>prāṇa</s> — by the previously stated principle, (SivSV 3.43:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * nisargāt sahajāt svasya svātantryād anivāritāt || SivSV_3.43:2 ||
body.translated_text: from one's own nature, naturally, from one's own freedom which is unrestricted, (SivSV 3.43:2)
with the desire to bring about the excellence of the variety of the moving manifold, (SivSV 3.43:3)

body.text: * saṃkocaṃ parigṛhṇānā saṃvid bhagavatī svayam || SivSV_3.43:4 ||
body.translated_text: the blessed consciousness itself, assuming contraction, (SivSV 3.43:4)
attains the stages of contracted cognizer-subjects and their respective <s>prāṇas</s>. (SivSV 3.43:5)

body.text: * uktam arthaṃ dṛḍhīkartuṃ saṃvādaḥ so 'yam atra tu || SivSV_3.43:6 ||
body.translated_text: To confirm the stated meaning, here is this concordant [citation]: (SivSV 3.43:6)

body.text: * yā sā śaktiḥ parā sūkṣmā vyāpinī nirmalā śivā || SivSV_3.43:7 ||
body.translated_text: That <s>Śakti</s> which is supreme, subtle, all-pervading, pure, and auspicious, (SivSV 3.43:7)
the mother of the circle of powers, whose nature is supreme bliss-nectar, (SivSV 3.43:8)
<s>Mahāghoreśvarī</s>, fierce, the maker of creation and dissolution, (SivSV 3.43:9)

body.text: * trivahaṃ trividhaṃ triṣṭhaṃ balāt kālaṃ prakarṣati || SivSV_3.43:10 ||
body.translated_text: she forcefully draws forth time — threefold in flow, threefold in kind, and threefold in station. (SivSV 3.43:10)

body.text: * iti vājasaneyāyām iyam eva citiḥ parā || SivSV_3.43:11 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Vājasaneyī</s> [tradition], this very supreme consciousness, (SivSV 3.43:11)
having previously descended by its own freedom into the <s>prāṇa</s>-form of the cognizer, (SivSV 3.43:12)
flowing through the three channels (<s>nāḍīs</s>) of the nature of moon, sun, and fire, (SivSV 3.43:13)
characterized by inhalation and exhalation, entering and exiting within and without, (SivSV 3.43:14)
drawing within itself time which is threefold — past, present, and so forth — (SivSV 3.43:15)

body.text: * karṣanty antar bahiś ceti kathyate kālakarṣiṇī || SivSV_3.43:16 ||
body.translated_text: both inwardly and outwardly — thus it is called the drawer of time (<s>kālakarṣiṇī</s>). (SivSV 3.43:16)

body.text: * tato naisargikas tasyāḥ prāṇasambandha āgataḥ || SivSV_3.43:17 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, its connection with <s>prāṇa</s> has come naturally. (SivSV 3.43:17)

body.text: * sthite 'pi prāṇasambandhe yas tadārūḍha āntarīm || SivSV_3.43:18 ||
body.translated_text: Even while the connection with <s>prāṇa</s> persists, one who, having ascended to that, reflects upon (SivSV 3.43:18)

body.text: * saṃvidaṃ vimṛśann āste sa lokottaratāṃ vrajet || SivSV_3.43:19 ||
body.translated_text: the inner awareness — that one would attain the transcendent state. (SivSV 3.43:19)
Thus, by way of summarizing the means, the great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>) says: (SivSV 3.43:20)
Through the practice of centering in the interior middle of the nose, what [use] here of the left, right, and <s>suṣumnā</s> [channels]? (SivS 3.44)

children.translated_text: Of the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) that are densely [distributed] from the eyes to the pores of the hair, (SivSV 3.44:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
in those which are primary, which support all [functions], (SivSV 3.44:2)
in the pathways of the left (<s>savya</s>), right (<s>apasavya</s>), and central (<s>suṣumna</s>) channels, always, (SivSV 3.44:3)
the <s>nāsikā</s> (nose) of the channels is the <s>prāṇaśakti</s> (vital power), flowing in a coiled manner, (SivSV 3.44:4)

body.text: * antar ity āntarī saṃvit tatsvarūpasya yat punaḥ || SivSV_3.44:5 ||
body.translated_text: 'inner' means the inner consciousness; and what is (SivSV 3.44:5)
its middle — the principal [reality], being the innermost of all, the ground of the universe, (SivSV 3.44:6)

body.text: * parāmarśamayaṃ rūpam uttīrṇaṃ tasya saṃyamāt || SivSV_3.44:7 ||
body.translated_text: the form that is of the nature of reflective awareness, transcendent — from its control (<s>saṃyama</s>), (SivSV 3.44:7)
arising from the excellence of contemplation, from the reflective awareness of self-knowledge, (SivSV 3.44:8)

body.text: * kim atra saṃyame vācyam iyam eva samāhitiḥ || SivSV_3.44:9 ||
body.translated_text: what need be said about this control? This very absorption (<s>samāhiti</s>), (SivSV 3.44:9)
shining brilliantly in all states, inwardly and continuously, (SivSV 3.44:10)
is experienced only by the <s>yogī</s> through uninterrupted attentiveness without emergence [from absorption]. (SivSV 3.44:11)

body.text: * mayy āveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate || SivSV_3.44:12 ||
body.translated_text: 'Those who fix their minds on Me and worship Me, ever united, (SivSV 3.44:12)

body.text: * śraddhayā parayopetās te me yuktatamā matāḥ || SivSV_3.44:13 ||
body.translated_text: endowed with supreme faith — they are considered by Me to be the most united' — (SivSV 3.44:13)
following the principle declared in the revered <s>Bhagavadgītā</s>, (SivSV 3.44:14)

children.translated_text: And again, of the nature of the unfolding of the stated nature of consciousness, (SivSV 3.45:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
for the supreme <s>yogī</s> who has ascended to the highest <s>yoga</s>, there would be (SivSV 3.45:2)

body.translated_text: 'again there would be' — the meaning of this statement is clearly this: (SivSV 3.45:3)

body.text: * yac chivatvam amuṣyoktaṃ nāpūrvaṃ tat tu yoginaḥ || SivSV_3.45:4 ||
body.translated_text: the <s>Śiva</s>-nature that has been stated is not something new for the <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 3.45:4)

body.translated_text: capable of apprehending it; therefore, through the sequential means that have been stated, (SivSV 3.45:7)

body.translated_text: his <s>Śiva</s>-nature becomes manifest — thus the auspicious [truth] was proclaimed by <s>Śiva</s>. (SivSV 3.45:8)

following the path of the commentary established by the revered <s>Kṣemarāja</s>, (SivSV 3.45:17)
